section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Overview of Our Business:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: We are a diversified healthcare services leader dedicated to advancing health outcomes for patients everywhere.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our teams partner with biopharma companies, care providers, pharmacies, manufacturers, governments, and others to deliver insights, products, and services to help make quality care more accessible and affordable.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: We implemented a new segment reporting structure commencing in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, which resulted in four reportable segments: North American Pharmaceutical, Oncology & Multispecialty, Prescription Technology Solutions, and Medical-Surgical Solutions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our former Norwegian operations were included in Other.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: All prior segment information has been recast to reflect our new segment structure and current period presentation.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our organizational structure also includes Corporate, which consists of income and expenses associated with administrative functions and projects, as well as the results of certain investments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: The factors for determining the reportable segments include the manner in which management evaluates the performance of the Company combined with the nature of individual business activities.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: We evaluate the performance of our operating segments on a number of measures, including revenues and operating profit before interest expense and income taxes.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: The following summarizes our four reportable segments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Refer to Financial Note 20, “Segments of Business,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for further information regarding our reportable segments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: North American Pharmaceutical segment provides distribution and logistics services for branded, generic, specialty, biosimilar, and over-the-counter pharmaceutical drugs along with other healthcare-related products to customers in the United States (“U.S.”) and Canada.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: In addition, the segment sells financial, operational, and clinical solutions to pharmacies (retail, hospital, alternate sites) and provides consulting, outsourcing, technological, and other services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: The U.S. distribution operations were previously included in the former U.S. Pharmaceutical reportable segment and the Canadian operations were previously included in the former International reportable segment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Oncology & Multispecialty segment includes provider solutions that encompass specialty drug distribution, group purchasing organizations, infusion services, direct to patient pharmacy capabilities, cell and gene therapy services with InspiroGene, technology solutions, practice consulting services, and vaccine distribution.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: In addition, the segment supports the U.S. Oncology Network, one of the largest networks of physician-led, integrated, community-based oncology practices dedicated to advancing high-quality, evidence-based cancer care in the U.S., and includes PRISM Vision Holdings, LLC (“PRISM Vision”), which drives patient outcomes in a retina and ophthalmology setting.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Combined with Sarah Cannon Research Institute and our technology business, Ontada, this segment provides research, insights, technologies, and services that address and improve cancer and specialty care.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: This segment was previously reflected in the former U.S. Pharmaceutical reportable segment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Prescription Technology Solutions segment combines automation and our ability to navigate the healthcare ecosystem to connect patients, pharmacies, providers, pharmacy benefit managers, health plans, and biopharma companies to address patients’ medication access, affordability, and adherence challenges.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Prescription Technology Solutions offers technology services, which includes electronic prior authorization, prescription price transparency, benefit insight, dispensing support services, and patient enrollment, in addition to third-party logistics, and wholesale distribution support across various therapeutic categories and temperature ranges to biopharma customers throughout the product lifecycle.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Medical-Surgical Solutions segment provides medical-surgical, laboratory, and pharmaceutical distribution, logistics, and other services to U.S. healthcare providers operating in the non-acute settings.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: These include ambulatory care environments, such as physician offices, surgery centers, and hospital reference labs, as well as extended care settings, including nursing homes, hospice and home health care agencies, government facilities, and online marketplaces and retailers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: This segment offers national brand medical-surgical products as well as our own line of more than 4,000 high-quality products through a network of distribution centers within the U.S.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: During fiscal 2026, we announced our intention to separate this segment into an independent company.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: As a part of the separation strategy, on April 20, 2026, we announced a definitive agreement under which funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. (“Apollo Funds”) will acquire approximately 13% minority ownership interest in our Medical‑Surgical Solutions segment through an investment of approximately $1.25 billion in the segment’s convertible preferred equity.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our former Norwegian operations, which provided distribution and services to wholesale and retail customers in Norway where we owned, partnered, or franchised with retail pharmacies, were included in Other.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: During fiscal 2026, we completed the transaction to sell our businesses in Norway (“Norway disposal group”).

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Overview of Our Business
text: This divestiture is further described in the “Business Acquisitions and Divestitures” section below.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenues
text: Revenues

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenues
text: Revenues increased for the year ended March 31, 2026 compared to the prior year largely due to market growth in our North American Pharmaceutical segment, including higher volumes primarily from retail national account customers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenues
text: Market growth includes growing drug utilization and newly launched products, partially offset by branded to generic drug conversion and branded pharmaceutical price decreases.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenues
text: Revenue growth was also favorably impacted by growth in our Oncology & Multispecialty segment primarily due to higher specialty pharmaceutical sales.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: Gross Profit

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: Gross profit increased for the year ended March 31, 2026 compared to the prior year primarily due to growth in our Oncology & Multispecialty segment, driven by the addition of providers in practice management and growth of specialty pharmaceuticals, and in our Prescription Technology Solutions segment driven by higher volumes.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: Gross profit for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 included gains of $23 million and $444 million, respectively, representing our share of antitrust legal settlements.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: We recognized these amounts within "Cost of sales" in the Consolidated Statements of Operations within our North American Pharmaceutical segment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: Gross profit for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 also included a last-in, first-out (“LIFO”) credit of $210 million and charge of $82 million, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: The LIFO credit in fiscal 2026 was primarily due to brand deflation compared to the prior year charge which was primarily due to brand inflation.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit
text: Refer to the “Critical Accounting Estimates” section included in this Financial Review for further information regarding the use of the LIFO method of accounting within our North American Pharmaceutical business.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Gross Profit

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: Restructuring Initiatives

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We recorded restructuring, impairment, and related charges of $245 million and $286 million for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: These charges were included in “Restructuring, impairment, and related charges, net” in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we approved an initiative within our Prescription Technology Solutions segment to increase operational efficiencies and cost optimization efforts, with the intent of aligning with our long-term strategy.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: This initiative includes headcount reductions, the exit or downsizing of certain facilities, and other costs.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We anticipate total charges between $200 million and $250 million, consisting primarily of employee severance and other employee-related costs, and facility and other exit-related costs, including long-lived asset impairments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We recorded immaterial charges in fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 associated with this initiative.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: This program is anticipated to be substantially complete by the end of fiscal 2029.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: During the second quarter of fiscal 2025, we approved enterprise-wide initiatives to modernize and accelerate our technology service operating model, which were intended to improve business continuity, compliance, operating efficiency, and advance investments to streamline the organization.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: These initiatives include cost reduction efforts and support other rationalization efforts within Corporate, and the Medical-Surgical Solutions and North American Pharmaceutical segments to help realize long-term sustainable growth.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We anticipate total charges related to these initiatives of $650 million to $700 million, consisting primarily of employee severance and other employee-related costs as well as facility, exit and other related costs, including long-lived asset impairments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: These programs are anticipated to be substantially complete in fiscal 2028.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: For the year ended March 31, 2026, we recorded charges of $170 million related to the initiatives, which primarily includes facility, exit and other related costs as well as severance and other employee-related costs recorded within “Restructuring, impairment, and related charges, net” in the Consolidated Statement of Operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: For the year ended March 31, 2025, we recorded charges of $240 million related to the initiatives, which primarily included severance and other employee-related costs as well as facility, exit and other related costs, including long-lived asset impairments recorded within “Restructuring, impairment, and related charges, net” in the Consolidated Statement of Operations, and $58 million for the year ended March 31, 2025 related to inventory impairments recorded within “Cost of sales” in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: Refer to Financial Note 3, “Restructuring, Impairment, and Related Charges, Net,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for more information.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > FOREIGN OPERATIONS

text: CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We consider an accounting estimate to be critical if the estimate requires us to make assumptions about matters based upon past experience and management’s judgment that were uncertain at the time the accounting estimate was made and if different estimates that we reasonably could have used in the current period, or changes in the accounting estimate that are reasonably likely to occur from period to period, could have a material impact on our financial condition or results from operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Below are the estimates that we believe are critical to the understanding of our operating results and financial condition.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Other accounting policies are described in Financial Note 1, “Significant Accounting Policies,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Because of the uncertainty inherent in such estimates, actual results may differ from these estimates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Allowances for Credit Losses: Our receivables primarily consist of short-term trade accounts receivable from customers that result from the sale of goods and services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We also provide customer financing arrangements to customers who purchase our products and services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Customer financing primarily relates to guarantees provided to our customers, or their creditors, regarding the repurchase of inventories.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We also provide financing to certain customers related to the purchase of pharmacies, which serve as collateral for the loans.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We estimate the receivables for which we do not expect full collection based on historical collection rates and specific knowledge regarding the current creditworthiness of our customers and record an allowance in our consolidated financial statements for these amounts.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We consider historical credit losses, the current economic environment, customer credit ratings, collections on past due amounts, legal disputes, and bankruptcies, as well as reasonable and supportable forecasts to develop our allowance for credit losses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Management reviews these factors quarterly to determine if any adjustments are needed to the allowance.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Sales to our ten largest customers, including group purchasing organizations (“GPOs”), accounted for approximately 73% of total consolidated revenues in fiscal 2026 and comprised approximately 43% of total trade accounts receivable at March 31, 2026.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Sales to our largest customer, CVS Health Corporation (“CVS”), accounted for approximately 24% of our total consolidated revenues in fiscal 2026 and comprised approximately 21% of total trade accounts receivable at March 31, 2026.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Sales to our next two largest customers accounted for 11% and 10% of total consolidated revenues in fiscal 2026.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: As a result, our sales and credit concentration is significant.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We also have agreements with GPOs, each of which functions as a purchasing agent on behalf of member hospitals, pharmacies and other healthcare providers, as well as with government entities and agencies.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The accounts receivable balances are with individual members of the GPOs, and therefore no significant concentration of credit risk exists.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: A material default in payment, a material reduction in purchases from GPOs or any other large customers, or the loss of a large customer or GPO could have a material adverse impact on our financial position, results of operations, and liquidity.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Reserve methodologies are assessed annually based on historical losses and economic, business, and market trends.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: In addition, reserves are reviewed quarterly and updated if unusual circumstances or trends are present.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We believe the reserves maintained and expenses recorded in fiscal 2026 are appropriate and consistent in the context of historical methodologies employed, as well as assessment of trends currently available.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: At March 31, 2026, trade and notes receivables were $24.5 billion prior to allowances of $204 million.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our provision for bad debts was a charge of $100 million, in fiscal 2026, a credit of $130 million in fiscal 2025, and a charge of $819 million in fiscal 2024, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: At March 31, 2026 and 2025, our allowance as a percentage of trade and notes receivables was 0.8% and 2.1%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The provision for bad debts for fiscal 2024 included a charge of $725 million within our North American Pharmaceutical segment related to the bankruptcy of our customer Rite Aid, as discussed in the Financial Note 20, “Segments of Business,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: This amount represented the uncollected trade accounts receivable balance due from Rite Aid prior to its bankruptcy petition filing in October 2023.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Inventories: Inventories consist of merchandise held for resale.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We report inventories at the lower of cost or net realizable value, except for inventories determined using the LIFO method which are valued at the lower of LIFO cost or market.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The LIFO method presumes that the most recent inventory purchases are the first items sold and the inventory cost under LIFO approximates market.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The majority of the cost of domestic inventories is determined using the LIFO method.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The majority of the cost of inventories held in foreign and certain domestic locations is based on the first-in, first-out (“FIFO”) method or weighted-average purchase prices.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Rebates, cash discounts, and other incentives received from vendors relating to the purchase or distribution of inventory are considered product discounts and are accounted for as a reduction in the cost of inventory and are recognized when the inventory is sold.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: In determining whether an inventory valuation allowance is required, we consider various factors including estimated quantities of slow-moving inventory by reviewing on-hand quantities, outstanding purchase obligations, and forecasted sales.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Shifts in market trends and conditions, changes in customer preferences due to the introduction of generic drugs or new pharmaceutical products, or the loss of one or more significant customers are factors that could affect the value of our inventories.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We write down inventories which are considered excess and obsolete as a result of these reviews.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These factors could make our estimates of inventory valuation differ from actual results.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We believe the moving-average inventory costing method reasonably approximates current replacement cost (“Market”).

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Accordingly, LIFO inventories are carried at the lower of LIFO cost or Market.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: At March 31, 2026 and 2025, inventories, net, totaled $24.2 billion and $23.0 billion, respectively, with approximately 59% and 63% valued using LIFO.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: At March 31, 2026 and 2025, our LIFO reserves were $99 million and $309 million.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: LIFO reserves include both pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical products.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: A LIFO charge is recognized when the net effect of price increases on pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical products held in inventory exceeds the impact of price declines, including the effect of branded pharmaceutical products that have lost market exclusivity.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: A LIFO credit is recognized when the net effect of price declines exceeds the impact of price increases on pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical products held in inventory.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We recognized a LIFO credit of $210 million in fiscal 2026, a LIFO charge of $82 million in fiscal 2025, and a LIFO credit of $157 million in fiscal 2024, all within “Cost of sales” in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The LIFO credit in fiscal 2026 compared to a LIFO charge in fiscal 2025 was primarily due to significant brand deflation in the current fiscal year, compared to the prior fiscal year brand inflation.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The LIFO charge in fiscal 2025 compared to a LIFO credit in fiscal 2024 was primarily due to higher brand inflation in fiscal 2025.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our LIFO valuation amount includes both pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical products.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Business Combinations: We account for business combinations using the acquisition method of accounting whereby the identifiable assets and liabilities of the acquired business, including contingent consideration, as well as any noncontrolling interest in the acquired business, are recorded at their estimated fair values as of the date that we obtain control of the acquired business.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Any purchase consideration in excess of the estimated fair values of the net assets acquired is recorded as goodwill.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Acquisition-related expenses and related costs are expensed as incurred.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Several valuation methods may be used to determine the fair value of assets acquired and liabilities assumed.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: For intangible assets, we typically use a variation of the income approach, whereby a forecast of future cash flows attributable to the asset is discounted to present value using a risk-adjusted discount rate.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Some of the more significant estimates and assumptions inherent in the income approach include the amount and timing of projected future cash flows, the discount rate selected to measure the risks inherent in the future cash flows, and the assessment of the asset’s expected useful life.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Refer to Financial Note 2, “Business Acquisitions and Divestitures,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information regarding our acquisitions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Certain business combinations involve the potential for future payments of consideration that is contingent upon the achievement of performance milestones or other agreed-upon events.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The liability for the contingent consideration is measured at its fair value as of the acquisition date using unobservable inputs.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These inputs include the estimated amount and timing of projected operational and financial information, the probability of achievement of performance milestones or other agreed-upon events, and the risk-adjusted discount rate used to calculate the present value of the probability-weighted projected financial information.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Contingent liabilities are remeasured to fair value at each reporting date until the liability is resolved with changes in fair value being recognized within “Selling, distribution, general, and administrative expenses” in the Consolidated Statements of Operations included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Changes in any of the inputs may result in a significant adjustment to the fair value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Long-Lived Assets
text: Goodwill and Long-Lived Assets:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: As a result of acquiring businesses, we have $11.3 billion and $10.0 billion of goodwill at March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively, and $4.1 billion and $1.5 billion of intangible assets, net at March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: We perform an impairment test on goodwill balances annually in the first fiscal quarter and more frequently if indicators for potential impairment exist.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Indicators that are considered include significant declines in performance relative to expected operating results, significant changes in the use of the assets, significant negative industry or economic trends, or a significant decline in the Company’s stock price and/or market capitalization for a sustained period of time.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill impairment testing is conducted at the reporting unit level, which is generally defined as an operating segment or a component, one level below our operating segments, for which discrete financial information is available and where segment management regularly reviews the operating results of that reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: We apply the goodwill impairment test by comparing the estimated fair value of a reporting unit to its carrying value and an impairment charge is recorded equal to the amount of excess carrying value above the estimated fair value, if any, but not to exceed the amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: To estimate the fair value of our reporting units, we generally use a combination of the market approach and the income approach.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Under the market approach, we estimate fair value by comparing the business to similar businesses, or guideline companies whose securities are actively traded in public markets.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Under the income approach, we use a discounted cash flow model in which cash flows anticipated over several periods, plus a terminal value at the end of that time horizon, are discounted to their present value using an appropriate rate that is commensurate with the risk inherent within the reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: In addition, we compare the aggregate of the reporting units’ fair values to our market capitalization as further corroboration of the reasonableness of our concluded fair values.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Estimates of fair value result from a complex series of judgments about future events and uncertainties and rely heavily on estimates and assumptions at a point in time.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Judgments made in determining an estimate of fair value may materially impact our results of operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: The valuations are based on information available as of the impairment testing date and are based on expectations and assumptions that have been deemed reasonable by management.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Any material changes in key assumptions, including failure to meet business plans, negative changes in government reimbursement rates, deterioration in the U.S. and global financial markets, an increase in interest rates, or an increase in the cost of equity financing by market participants within the industry, or other unanticipated events and circumstances may decrease the projected cash flows or increase the discount rates and could potentially result in an impairment charge.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Under the market approach, significant estimates and assumptions also include the selection of appropriate guideline public companies and the determination of appropriate valuation multiples to apply to the reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Under the income approach, significant estimates and assumptions also include the determination of discount rates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: The discount rates represent the weighted-average cost of capital measuring the reporting unit’s cost of debt and equity financing, which are weighted by the percentage of debt and percentage of equity in a company’s target capital structure.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Included in the estimate of the weighted-average cost of capital is the assumption of an unsystematic risk premium to address incremental uncertainty related to the reporting unit’s future cash flow projections.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: The annual impairment testing performed for fiscal 2026, fiscal 2025, and fiscal 2024 did not indicate any impairment of goodwill.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Refer to Financial Note 10, “Goodwill and Intangible Assets, Net,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Long-Lived Assets

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Currently, all of our identifiable intangible and other long-lived assets are amortized or depreciated based on the pattern of their economic consumption or a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, ranging from three to 26 years.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We review intangible and other long-lived assets for impairment at an asset group level whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying value of the assets may not be recoverable.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Determination of recoverability of intangible and other long-lived assets is based on the lowest level of identifiable estimated future undiscounted cash flows resulting from the use of the asset and its eventual disposition.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Measurement of any impairment loss is based on the excess of the carrying value of the asset group over its fair value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Assumptions and estimates about future values and the remaining useful lives of our purchased intangible assets are complex and subjective.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: They can be affected by a variety of factors, including external factors such as industry and economic trends, and internal factors such as changes in our business strategy and our internal forecasts.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Our ongoing consideration of all the factors described previously could result in further impairment charges in the future, which could adversely affect our net income.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Refer to Financial Note 3, “Restructuring, Impairment, and Related Charges, Net,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information on our long-lived asset impairments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Long-lived assets classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of their carrying amount or fair value less costs to sell and are not depreciated or amortized.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Fair value is determined based on the total consideration expected to be received by the Company.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: The fair value of a disposal group, less any costs to sell, is assessed each reporting period it remains classified as held for sale and any remeasurement to the lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell is reported as an adjustment to the carrying value of the disposal group.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: When the net realizable value of a disposal group increases during a period, a gain can be recognized to the extent that it does not increase the value of the disposal group beyond its original carrying value when the disposal group was reclassified as held for sale.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Restructuring Charges: We have certain restructuring reserves which require significant estimates related to the timing and amount of future employee severance and other exit-related costs to be incurred when the restructuring actions take place.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We generally recognize employee severance costs when payments are probable and amounts can be reasonably estimated.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Costs related to contracts without future benefit or contract termination are recognized at the earlier of the contract termination or the cease-use dates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Other exit-related costs are expensed as incurred.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: In connection with these restructuring actions, we also assess the recoverability of long-lived assets used in the business, and as a result, we may recognize accelerated depreciation and amortization reflecting shortened useful lives of the underlying assets.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Refer to Financial Note 3, “Restructuring, Impairment, and Related Charges, Net,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information on restructuring matters.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Income Taxes: Our income tax expense and deferred tax assets and liabilities reflect management’s best assessment of estimated current and future taxes to be paid.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We are subject to income taxes in the U.S. and numerous foreign jurisdictions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Significant judgments and estimates are required in determining the consolidated income tax provision and in evaluating income tax uncertainties, including those used to conclude on the unrecognized tax position related to opioid-related litigation and claims, and may differ from the actual amounts of tax benefit recognized.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We review our tax positions at the end of each quarter and adjust the balances as new information becomes available.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Deferred income taxes arise from temporary differences between the tax and financial statement recognition of revenue and expense.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: In evaluating our ability to recover our deferred tax assets, we consider all available positive and negative evidence including our past operating results, the existence of cumulative net operating losses in the most recent years, and our forecast of future taxable income.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: In estimating future taxable income, we develop assumptions including the amount of future federal, state, and foreign pre-tax operating income, the reversal of temporary differences, and the implementation of feasible and prudent tax planning strategies.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: These assumptions require significant judgment about the forecasts of future taxable income and are consistent with the plans and estimates we use to manage the underlying businesses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Changes in tax laws and rates could also affect recorded deferred tax assets and liabilities in the future.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Should tax laws change, our tax expense and cash flows could be materially impacted.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: In addition, the calculation of our tax liabilities includes estimates for uncertainties in the application of complex new tax regulations across multiple global jurisdictions where we conduct our operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We recognize liabilities for tax and related interest for issues in the U.S. and other tax jurisdictions based on our estimate of whether, and the extent to which, additional taxes and related interest will be due.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: If our current estimate of tax and interest liabilities is less than the ultimate settlement, an additional charge to income tax expense may result.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: If our current estimate of tax and interest liabilities is more than the ultimate settlement, a reduction to income tax expense may be recognized.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Refer to Financial Note 6, “Income Taxes,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information on income tax matters.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Loss Contingencies: We are subject to various claims, including claims with customers and vendors, pending and potential legal actions for damages, investigations relating to laws and regulations and other matters arising out of the normal conduct of our business.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: When a loss is considered probable and reasonably estimable, we record a liability in the amount of our best estimate for the ultimate loss.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: However, the likelihood of a loss with respect to a particular contingency is often difficult to predict, and determining a meaningful estimate of the loss or a range of loss may not be practicable based on the information available and the potential effect of future events and decisions by third parties that will determine the ultimate resolution of the contingency.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Moreover, it is not uncommon for such matters to be resolved over many years, during which time relevant developments and new information must be reevaluated at least quarterly to determine both the likelihood of potential loss and whether it is possible to reasonably estimate a range of possible loss.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: When a material loss is reasonably possible, or probable but a reasonable estimate cannot be made, disclosure of the proceeding is provided.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Legal fees are expensed as incurred when the legal services are provided.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We review all contingencies at least quarterly to determine whether the likelihood of loss has changed and to assess whether a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of the loss can be made.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: As discussed above, development of a meaningful estimate of loss or a range of potential loss is complex when the outcome is directly dependent on future negotiations with or decisions by third parties, such as regulatory agencies, the court system, and other interested parties.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: In conjunction with the preparation of the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report, we considered matters related to ongoing controlled substances claims to which we are a party.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: At March 31, 2026, our estimated accrued liability for opioid-related claims was $5.7 billion.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We are not able to reasonably estimate the upper or lower ends of the range of ultimate possible losses for all opioid-related litigation matters.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: We are not able to predict the outcome in these matters, and an adverse judgment or negotiated resolution in any of these matters could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial position, and cash flows or liquidity.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Long-Lived Assets
text: Refer to Financial Note 17, “Commitments and Contingent Liabilities,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report for additional information.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: Operating Activities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: Operating activities provided cash of $6.2 billion and $6.1 billion for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: Cash flows from operations can be significantly impacted by factors such as the timing of receipts from customers, inventory receipts, and payments to vendors.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: Additionally, working capital is primarily a function of sales and purchase volumes, inventory requirements, and vendor payment terms.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: For the year ended March 31, 2026, net cash provided by operating activities increased by $70 million compared to the prior year period.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: This increase was primarily due to the following:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: the Company’s net income increased by $1.6 billion and was impacted by lower net non-cash items of $836 million, compared to the prior year period driven by factors discussed in more detail in the “Overview of Consolidated Results” section of this Financial Review;

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: an increase in net cash of $1.9 billion related to accounts receivable primarily due to favorable timing of collections in the current period and the impact from branded pharmaceutical price decreases;

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: a decrease in net cash of $4.0 billion related to accounts payable as a result of customary vendor payment scheduling, timing related to the day of the week on which the period ends, and the impact from branded pharmaceutical price decreases, partially offset by an increase in net cash of $1.2 billion due to higher inventory requirements during the period compared to the prior year; and

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Operating Activities
text: an increase in net cash from other assets and liabilities primarily related to lower contract liability and customer rebate payments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing Activities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities used cash of $3.4 billion and $733 million for the years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities for the March 31, 2026 included $3.4 billion of net cash payments for acquisitions, including $2.5 billion and $875 million for the acquisitions of the interests in Core Ventures and PRISM Vision, respectively, as discussed in further detail in Financial Note 2, “Business Acquisitions and Divestitures,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities for the year ended March 31, 2026 were also impacted by the receipt of proceeds from sales of businesses and investments of $830 million, including cash proceeds, net of cash divested, of $693 million from the completed divestiture of our Norway disposal group, as discussed in Financial Note 2, “Business Acquisitions and Divestitures,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities for the year ended March 31, 2026 included $436 million and $309 million, respectively, in capital expenditures for property, plant, and equipment and capitalized software.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities for the year ended March 31, 2025 included $537 million and $322 million, respectively, in capital expenditures for property, plant, and equipment and capitalized software.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Investing Activities
text: Investing activities for the year ended March 31, 2025 were also impacted by the receipt of proceeds of $189 million related to investments in equity securities, as discussed in Financial Note 15, “Fair Value Measurements,” to the consolidated financial statements included in this Annual Report.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Overview of Our Business:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: We are a diversified healthcare services leader dedicated to advancing health outcomes for patients everywhere.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our teams partner with biopharma companies, care providers, pharmacies, manufacturers, governments, and others to deliver insights, products, and services to help make quality care more accessible and affordable.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: We implemented a new segment reporting structure commencing in the second quarter of fiscal 2026, which resulted in four reportable segments: North American Pharmaceutical, Oncology & Multispecialty, Prescription Technology Solutions, and Medical-Surgical Solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our former Norwegian operations were included in Other.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: All prior segment information has been recast to reflect our new segment structure and current period presentation.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Our organizational structure also includes Corporate, which consists of income and expenses associated with administrative functions and projects, as well as the results of certain investments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: The factors for determining the reportable segments include the manner in which management evaluates the performance of the Company combined with the nature of individual business activities.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: We evaluate the performance of our reportable segments on a number of measures, including revenues and operating profit before interest expense and income taxes.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: The following summarizes our four reportable segments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Refer to Financial Note 13, “Segments of Business,” to the accompanying condensed consolidated financial statements included in this Quarterly Report for further information regarding our reportable segments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: North American Pharmaceutical segment provides distribution and logistics services for branded, generic, specialty, biosimilar, and over-the-counter pharmaceutical drugs along with other healthcare-related products to customers in the United States (“U.S.”) and Canada.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: In addition, the segment sells financial, operational, and clinical solutions to pharmacies (retail, hospital, alternate sites) and provides consulting, outsourcing, technological, and other services.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Oncology & Multispecialty segment includes provider solutions that encompass specialty drug distribution, group purchasing organizations, infusion services, direct to patient pharmacy capabilities, cell and gene therapy services with InspiroGene, technology solutions, practice consulting services, and vaccine distribution.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: In addition, the segment supports The U.S. Oncology Network, one of the largest networks of physician-led, integrated, community-based oncology practices dedicated to advancing high-quality, evidence-based cancer care in the U.S., and includes PRISM Vision Holdings, LLC (“PRISM Vision”), which drives patient outcomes in a retina and ophthalmology setting.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Combined with Sarah Cannon Research Institute and our technology business, Ontada, this segment provides research, insights, technologies, and services that address and improve cancer and specialty care.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Prescription Technology Solutions segment combines automation and our ability to navigate the healthcare ecosystem to connect patients, pharmacies, providers, pharmacy benefit managers, health plans, and biopharma companies to address patients’ medication access, affordability, and adherence challenges.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Prescription Technology Solutions offers technology services, which includes electronic prior authorization, prescription price transparency, benefit insight, dispensing support services, and patient enrollment, in addition to third-party logistics, and wholesale distribution support across various therapeutic categories and temperature ranges to biopharma customers throughout the product lifecycle.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: Medical-Surgical Solutions segment provides medical-surgical, laboratory, and pharmaceutical distribution, logistics, and other services to U.S. healthcare providers operating in the non-acute settings.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: These include ambulatory care environments, such as physician offices, surgery centers, and hospital reference labs, as well as extended care settings, including nursing homes, hospice and home health care agencies, government facilities, and online marketplaces and retailers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: This segment offers national brand medical-surgical products as well as our own line of more than 4,000 high-quality products through a network of distribution centers within the U.S.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: During fiscal 2026, we announced our intention to separate this segment into an independent company.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: As a part of the separation strategy, on June 1, 2026, we completed a transaction under which funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management, Inc. (“Apollo Funds”) acquired an approximately 13% minority ownership interest in our Medical‑Surgical Solutions segment through an investment of approximately $1.25 billion in the segment’s convertible preferred equity.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: We recognized a redeemable noncontrolling interest associated with the divested portion of the Medical‑Surgical Solutions segment.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview of Our Business
text: We retain operating control and majority ownership of Medical-Surgical Solutions and continue to consolidate this segment into our consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, we approved multi-year initiatives within Corporate to further optimize its operating model and align certain enterprise support functions with our long-term strategic priorities.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: These initiatives include organizational changes, process enhancements, and the implementation of automation solutions designed to improve efficiency and productivity.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We anticipate total charges of approximately $230 million to $310 million, consisting primarily of severance and employee-related costs and exit-related costs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we approved an initiative within our Prescription Technology Solutions segment to increase operational efficiencies and cost optimization efforts, with the intent of aligning with our long-term strategy.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: This initiative includes headcount reductions, the exit or downsizing of certain facilities, and other costs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We anticipate total charges between $200 million and $250 million, consisting primarily of employee severance and other employee-related costs, and facility and other exit-related costs, including long-lived asset impairments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives
text: We recorded charges of $61 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 associated with this initiative, which primarily includes asset impairments as well as severance and other employee-related costs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Restructuring Initiatives

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Item 1. Business

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Medtronic plc, headquartered in Galway, Ireland, is the leading global healthcare technology company.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Medtronic was founded in 1949 and today serves healthcare systems, physicians, clinicians, and patients in more than 150 countries worldwide.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: We remain committed to a mission written by our founder in 1960 that directs us “to contribute to human welfare by the application of biomedical engineering in the research, design, manufacture, and sale of products to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life.”

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Our Mission — to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life — empowers us to engineer the extraordinary and deliver better outcomes for our world.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: We are a company of dedication, honesty, integrity, and service.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Building on this strong foundation, we are embracing our role as a healthcare technology leader and evolving our business strategy in three key areas:

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Accelerate innovation-driven growth: The combination of our attractive end markets, recent product launches and robust pipeline is expected to enable continued strong revenue growth.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: We aim to bring inventive and disruptive technology to large healthcare opportunities which enables us to better meet patient needs.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Patients around the world deserve access to our life-saving products, and we are driven to use our local presence and scale to increase the adoption of our products and services in markets around the globe.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Deliver superior outcomes and better experiences for patients and providers: We listen to our patients and customers to better understand the challenges they face.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: From the patient journey, to creating agile partnerships that produce novel solutions, to making it easier for our customers to deploy our therapies — what we do is anchored in deep insight, and creates simpler, superior experiences.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: Turn data, AI, and automation into action: We are confident in our ability to maximize new technology, AI, and data and analytics to tailor therapies in real-time, facilitating remote monitoring and care delivery that conveniently manages conditions, and creates new standards of care.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: We have three reportable segments that primarily develop, manufacture, distribute, and sell device-based medical therapies and services: the Cardiovascular Portfolio, the Neuroscience Portfolio, and the Medical Surgical Portfolio.

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: In May 2025, the Company announced its intent to separate the Diabetes Business, with the intention to create a new independent, publicly traded company, MiniMed Group, Inc. (MiniMed).

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: On March 9, 2026, MiniMed completed an initial public offering (the IPO).

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: As a result, during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, the Diabetes Operating Unit was no longer considered a reportable segment.
