text: On July 4, 2025, the U.S. Government enacted The One Big Beautiful Bill Act of 2025, which includes, among other provisions, changes to the U.S. corporate income tax system including the allowance of immediate expensing of qualifying research and development expenses and permanent extensions of certain provisions within the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > INCOME TAXES
text: The provisions of the Act, including immediate expensing of qualifying research and development costs, that were effective for fiscal year 2026 did not materially impact the Company's fiscal year 2026 effective tax rate.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > INCOME TAXES
text: The Company does not expect the provisions of the Act to materially impact fiscal years 2027 and beyond.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > INCOME TAXES
text: The Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) published Pillar Two Model Rules defining the global minimum tax, which calls for the taxation of large multinational corporations at a minimum rate of 15% in each jurisdiction in which the group operates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > INCOME TAXES
text: The OECD has since issued administrative guidance providing transition and safe harbor rules around the implementation of the Pillar Two Model Rules.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > INCOME TAXES
text: A number of countries, including Ireland, have enacted legislation to implement the core elements of Pillar Two Model Rules, which were effective for Medtronic in fiscal year 2025.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We have used various accounting policies to prepare the consolidated financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our significant accounting policies are disclosed in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The preparation of the consolidated financial statements, in conformity with U.S. GAAP, requires us to use judgment in making estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These estimates reflect our best judgment about economic and market conditions and the potential effects on the valuation and/or carrying value of assets and liabilities based upon relevant information available.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We base our estimates on historical experience and on various assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our critical accounting estimates include the following:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Revenue Recognition Revenue recognition on our products varies depending on the amount of consideration we ultimately receive due to return terms, sales rebates, chargebacks, discounts, and other incentives, which are accounted for as variable consideration.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The estimate of variable consideration for rebates and distributor chargebacks is considered critical due to the materiality of the balances and use of estimates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Estimates for rebates are based on sales terms, historical experience, and trend analysis.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The Company considers the lag time between the point of sale and payment of the rebate claim, the stated rebate rates, and other relevant information to estimate rebates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Revenue adjustments related to distributor chargebacks are the difference between distributor sales price and the end-customer negotiated price.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: A provision for outstanding chargebacks is recorded when we recognize revenue from our sale to the distributor and requires estimates for the distributor chargeback rate, expected sell-through levels by the distributors to contracted customers, as well as estimated distributor inventory levels.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: At April 24, 2026 and April 25, 2025, there were $1.9 billion and $2.0 billion of rebates, chargebacks, and other adjustments recorded in the consolidated balance sheets, respectively.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: During fiscal years 2026 and 2025, adjustments to rebates, chargebacks, and other adjustments recorded in prior periods were not material.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Litigation Contingencies We are involved in a number of legal actions from time to time involving product liability, employment, intellectual property and commercial disputes, shareholder-related matters, environmental proceedings, tax disputes, and governmental proceedings and investigations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The outcomes of legal actions are not within the Company's complete control and may not be known for prolonged periods of time.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: In some actions, the enforcement agencies or private claimants seek damages, as well as other civil or criminal remedies (including injunctions barring the sale of products that are the subject of the proceeding), that could require significant expenditures, result in lost revenues, or limit the Company's ability to conduct business in the applicable jurisdictions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Estimating probable losses from our litigation and governmental proceedings is inherently difficult, particularly when the matters are in early procedural stages, with incomplete scientific facts or legal discovery, involve unsubstantiated or indeterminate claims for damages, potentially involve penalties, fines, or punitive damages, or could result in a change in business practice.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We base our judgments on the best information available at the time.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our estimates related to our legal and product liability accruals may change as additional information becomes available to us, including information related to the nature or existence of claims against us, trial court or appellate proceedings, and mediation, arbitration or settlement proceedings.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Any revision of our estimates of potential liability could have a material impact on our financial position and operating results.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our significant legal proceedings are discussed in Note 18 to the consolidated financial statements in "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Income Tax Reserves We establish reserves when, despite our belief that our tax return positions are fully supportable, we believe that certain positions are likely to be challenged and that we may or may not prevail.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Under U.S. GAAP, if we determine that a tax position is more likely than not of being sustained upon audit, based solely on the technical merits of the position, we recognize the benefit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We measure the benefit by determining the amount that is greater than 50 percent likely of being realized upon settlement.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We presume that all tax positions will be examined by a taxing authority with full knowledge of all relevant information.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The calculation of our tax liabilities involves dealing with uncertainties in the application of complex tax regulations in a multitude of jurisdictions across our global operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We regularly monitor our tax positions and tax liabilities.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We reevaluate the technical merits of our tax positions and recognize an uncertain tax benefit, or derecognize a previously recorded tax benefit, when there is (i) a completion of a tax audit, (ii) effective settlement of an issue, (iii) a change in applicable tax law including a tax case or legislative guidance, or (iv) the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These reserves are subject to a high degree of estimation and management judgment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Although we believe that we have adequately reserved for liabilities resulting from tax assessments by taxing authorities, positions taken by these tax authorities could have a material impact on our effective tax rate, consolidated earnings, financial position, and/or cash flows.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Valuation of Intangible Assets and Goodwill When we acquire a business, the assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recorded at their respective fair values at the acquisition date.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Goodwill is the excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair value of identified net assets of acquired businesses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Intangible assets primarily include patents, trademarks, tradenames, customer relationships, purchased technology, and in-process research and development.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Determining the fair value of intangible assets acquired as part of a business combination requires us to make significant estimates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These estimates include the amount and timing of projected future cash flows of each project or technology, the discount rate used to discount those cash flows to present value, and the assessment of the asset’s life cycle.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The estimates could be impacted by legal, technical, regulatory, economic, and competitive risks.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Goodwill and indefinite lived intangible assets are tested for impairment annually in the third quarter of the fiscal year and whenever an event occurs or circumstances change that would indicate the carrying amount may be impaired.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Intangible assets with a definite life are tested for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset group, which includes intangible assets, may not be recoverable.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: If goodwill or intangible assets are determined to be impaired, they are written down to their estimated fair value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We have four goodwill reporting units with goodwill assigned to them.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The test for impairment of goodwill requires us to make several estimates related to projected future cash flows to determine the fair value of the goodwill reporting units.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We estimated the fair value of these reporting units using the income and the market approaches, weighted 50 percent each.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Fair value under the income approach was determined by discounting to present value the estimated future cash flows of the reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Fair value under the market approach utilized revenue and earnings multiples using comparable public company information, which uses valuation indicators determined from other businesses that are similar to our reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We use estimates that are consistent with the highest and best use of the assets based on a market participant's view of the assets being evaluated.

text: The fair value of the reporting unit’s goodwill is sensitive to differences between estimated and actual cash flows, including changes in the projected revenue, projected earnings, and discount rate used to evaluate the fair value of the reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: As part of our annual impairment analysis in the third quarter, we completed a quantitative impairment analysis of all of our reporting units to determine if their fair value was less than their carrying amount.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: Financial Trends

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: Throughout this Management’s Discussion and Analysis, we present certain financial measures that facilitate management's review of the operational performance of the Company and as a basis for strategic planning; however, such financial measures are not presented in our financial statements prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (U.S.) (U.S. GAAP).

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: These financial measures are considered non-GAAP financial measures and are intended to supplement, and should not be considered as superior to, financial measures presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: We believe that non-GAAP financial measures provide information useful to investors in understanding the Company's underlying operational performance and trends and may facilitate comparisons with the performance of other companies in the medical technologies industry.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: As presented in the "GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliations" section on the following pages, our non-GAAP financial measures exclude the impact of amortization of intangible assets and certain charges or benefits that contribute to or reduce earnings and that may affect financial trends.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: These measures include certain charges or benefits that result from transactions or events that we believe may or may not recur with similar materiality or impact our operations in future periods (non-GAAP adjustments).

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: In the event there is a non-GAAP adjustment recognized in our operating results, the tax cost or benefit attributable to that item is separately calculated and reported.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: Because the effective rate can be significantly impacted by the non-GAAP adjustments that take place during the period, we often refer to our tax rate using both the effective rate and the non-GAAP nominal tax rate.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: The non-GAAP nominal tax rate is calculated as the income tax provision, adjusted for the impact of non-GAAP adjustments, as a percentage of income before income taxes, excluding non-GAAP adjustments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: Free cash flow, a non-GAAP financial measure, is calculated by subtracting additions to property, plant, and equipment from net cash provided by operating activities.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Financial Trends
text: Refer to the "GAAP to Non-GAAP Reconciliations," "Income Taxes," and "Free Cash Flow" sections for reconciliations of the non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable financial measures prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: Macroeconomic Trends

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: Looking ahead, a number of macroeconomic and geopolitical factors could negatively impact our business, including without limitation:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: Competitive product launches and pricing pressure, geographic macroeconomic developments including changes in global trade policies and fluctuations in currency exchange rates, general price inflation, changes in interest rates, reimbursement challenges, impacts from changes in the mix of our product offerings, delays in product registration approvals, national and provincial tender pricing for certain products, particularly in China, replacement cycle challenges, and supply chain challenges from time to time.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: Recent developments in global trade policy have introduced new uncertainties for our business.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: The U.S., China, and other jurisdictions have recently imposed or proposed additional tariffs on imported goods.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: While we are taking proactive steps to mitigate the effects of these tariffs, the evolving nature of international trade policy continues to present a risk to our cost structure and financial performance.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that President Trump's tariff policies under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") are unconstitutional.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: Following that ruling, U.S. Customs and Border Protection ("CBP") implemented procedures for the processing of IEEPA tariff refunds, and the Company has participated in those processes where appropriate.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: We continue to monitor developments in global trade policy, including changes to tariff regimes and related administrative actions.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: The impact of such developments, including further escalation or expansion of trade barriers, could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: The planned exit of certain businesses, including our Diabetes Business, may involve separation activities, costs, and risks associated with transitioning operations, arrangements, and infrastructure.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Macroeconomic Trends
text: The timing and execution of these activities, as well as any related disposition steps, could affect our future results and financial condition.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Cardiovascular
text: Cardiovascular

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Cardiovascular
text: Cardiovascular products include pacemakers, insertable cardiac monitors, cardiac resynchronization therapy devices, implantable cardioverter defibrillators, leads and delivery systems, products for the treatment of atrial fibrillation, information systems for the management of patients with Electrophysiology Therapy devices, products designed to reduce surgical site infections, coronary and peripheral stents and related delivery systems, balloons and related delivery systems, endovascular stent graft systems, heart valve replacement technologies, cardiac tissue ablation systems, open heart and coronary bypass grafting surgical products, and renal denervation systems for the treatment of hypertension.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Cardiovascular
text: Cardiovascular also includes Care Management Services and Cath Lab Managed Services (CLMS) within the Electrophysiology Therapies division.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Cardiovascular
text: Cardiovascular's net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 were $3.9 billion, an increase of 20 percent, as compared to the corresponding period in the prior fiscal year, resulting from growth across most businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Neuroscience
text: Neuroscience

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Neuroscience
text: Neuroscience's products include various spinal implants, bone graft substitutes, biologic products, image-guided surgery and intra-operative imaging systems, robotic guidance systems used in the robot-assisted spine procedures, and systems that incorporate advanced energy surgical instruments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Neuroscience
text: Neuroscience's products also focus on therapies to treat the diseases of the vasculature in and around the brain, including coils, neurovascular stents, and flow diversion products, as well as products to treat the ear, nose, and throat (ENT), and the treatment of overactive bladder and urinary retention.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Neuroscience
text: Neuroscience also manufactures products related to implantable neurostimulation therapies and drug delivery systems for the treatment of chronic pain, movement disorders, and epilepsy.

text: Neuroscience’s net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was $2.7 billion, an increase of 10 percent, as compared to the corresponding period in the prior fiscal year, resulting from growth across most businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Medical Surgical

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Medical Surgical’s products span the entire continuum of patient care from diagnosis to recovery, with a focus on diseases of the gastrointestinal tract, lungs, pelvic region, obesity, and preventable complications.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The products include those for advanced and general surgical products, surgical stapling devices, vessel sealing instruments, wound closure, electrosurgery products, hernia mechanical devices, mesh implants, advanced ablation, interventional lung, airway products, and sensors and monitors for pulse oximetry, capnography, level of consciousness and cerebral oximetry.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Medical Surgical's net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 was $2.3 billion, an increase of 10 percent as compared to the corresponding period in the prior fiscal year, resulting from growth across most businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The graphs below illustrate the percent of Medical Surgical net sales by division for the three months ended July 31, 2026 and July 25, 2025:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Surgical & Endoscopy (SE) net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 increased 9 percent as compared to the corresponding period in the prior fiscal year.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The net sales increase was primarily due to growth in Surgical, with strength in LigaSure vessel sealing technology, V-Loc barbed sutures, ProGrip self-gripping polyester mesh, Hugo robotic assisted surgery (RAS) system, and Endoscopy.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Acute Care & Monitoring (ACM) net sales for the three months ended July 31, 2026 increased 14 percent as compared to the corresponding period in the prior fiscal year.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The net sales increase was primarily due to growth in Nellcor pulse oximetry and McGRATH MAC video laryngoscope, and Microstream Capnography.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: In addition to the macroeconomic and geopolitical factors described in the Executive Level Overview, looking ahead we expect Medical Surgical could be affected by the following:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Acceptance and continued growth of Open-to-MIS (minimally invasive surgery) techniques and tools through our efforts to transition open surgery to MIS.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Open-to-MIS initiative focuses on capturing the market opportunity that exists in transitioning open procedures to MIS, whether through traditional MIS, advanced instrumentation, or robotics.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Through our approach, in parallel, we also expand our presence and optimize open surgery in current open surgery markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Continued global acceptance and future growth of powered stapling and energy platform.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Our ability to execute ongoing strategies addressing the pressures to bariatric surgery procedure volumes in the U.S. from pharmaceuticals, and growth of surgical soft tissue robotics procedures in the U.S.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Our ability to create markets and drive products and procedures into emerging markets with our high quality and cost-effective surgical products designed for customers in emerging markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Continued acceptance and growth in patient monitoring and airway management.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Key products in this area include Microstream Capnography, Nellcor pulse oximetry system with OxiMax technology, Shiley tracheostomy and endotracheal tubes, and McGRATH MAC video laryngoscopes.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Acceptance of less invasive standards of care in chronic and colorectal, as well as hepatology products, including products that span the care continuum from diagnostics to therapeutics.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Expanding the use of less invasive treatments and furthering our commitment to improving options for women with abnormal uterine bleeding.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Our expanded and strengthened surgical offerings complement our global gynecology business.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Global adoption of robotic-assisted surgery and the safe and effective use of the Hugo RAS system, including system reliability and acceptability, for urologic, bariatric, gynecologic, hernia, and general surgery procedures.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: This includes continued integration and adoption of Touch Surgery Enterprise with the first artificial intelligence (AI) powered surgical videos and analytics platform to make it easier to analyze performance, train, and discover new techniques within the robotics platform.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The Hugo RAS system is designed to help reduce unwanted variability, improve patient outcomes, and, by extension, lower per procedure cost.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: LigaSure RAS vessel-sealing technology received CE Mark in July 2025, expanding Hugo RAS system capabilities for gynecologic, general, and urologic procedures.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: The Hugo RAS system received U.S. FDA clearance for use in urologic surgical procedures in December 2025.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Medical Surgical
text: Our ability to meet growing demand for our existing products and to successfully develop, obtain regulatory approval of, and commercialize the products within our pipeline, which includes future indications and instrument expansions for our Hugo RAS system in the U.S. and the adoption of AI in Endoscopy and Digital Surgical Technologies.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We have used various accounting policies to prepare the condensed consolidated financial statements in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our significant accounting policies are disclosed in Note 1 to the consolidated financial statements included in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended April 24, 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The preparation of the condensed consolidated financial statements, in conformity with U.S. GAAP, requires us to use judgment in making estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These estimates reflect our best judgment about economic and market conditions and the potential effects on the valuation and/or carrying value of assets and liabilities based upon relevant information available.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We base our estimates on historical experience and on various assumptions that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities that are not readily apparent from other sources.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our critical accounting estimates are more fully described in Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended April 24, 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Valuation of Intangible Assets and Goodwill When we acquire a business, the assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recorded at their respective fair values at the acquisition date.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Goodwill is the excess of the purchase price over the estimated fair value of identified net assets of acquired businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Intangible assets primarily include patents, trademarks, tradenames, customer relationships, purchased technology, and in-process research and development.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Determining the fair value of intangible assets acquired as part of a business combination requires us to make significant estimates.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: These estimates include the amount and timing of projected future cash flows of each project or technology, the discount rate used to discount those cash flows to present value, and the assessment of the asset’s life cycle.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The estimates could be impacted by legal, technical, regulatory, economic, and competitive risks.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Goodwill and indefinite lived intangible assets are tested for impairment annually in the third quarter of the fiscal year and whenever an event occurs or circumstances change that would indicate the carrying amount may be impaired.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Intangible assets with a definite life are tested for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset group, which includes intangible assets, may not be recoverable.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: If goodwill or intangible assets are determined to be impaired, they are written down to their estimated fair value.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We have four goodwill reporting units with goodwill assigned to them.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The test for impairment of goodwill requires us to make several estimates related to projected future cash flows to determine the fair value of the goodwill reporting units.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We estimated the fair value of these reporting units using the income and the market approaches, weighted 50 percent each.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Fair value under the income approach was determined by discounting to present value the estimated future cash flows of the reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Fair value under the market approach utilized revenue and earnings multiples using comparable public company information, which uses valuation indicators determined from other businesses that are similar to our reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: We use estimates that are consistent with the highest and best use of the assets based on a market participant's view of the assets being evaluated.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The most critical assumptions used in the calculation of the fair value of each reporting unit are the projected revenue, projected earnings, projected future cash flows, and discount rate.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our forecast of future cash flows is based on estimates of projected revenue and projected earnings, based primarily on pricing, raw material costs, market share, industry outlook, general economic conditions and strategic actions to improve our earnings.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The fair value of the reporting unit’s goodwill is sensitive to differences between estimated and actual cash flows, including changes in the projected revenue, projected earnings, and discount rate used to evaluate the fair value of the reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: As part of our annual impairment analysis in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026, we completed a quantitative impairment analysis of all of our reporting units to determine if their fair value was less than their carrying amount.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Based on the quantitative test, the Medical Surgical reporting unit had an estimated fair value that exceeded its carrying value, including goodwill, by approximately 12%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: As of July 31, 2026, $19.7 billion of goodwill was allocated to the Medical Surgical reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: The remaining reporting units' fair values materially exceeded their carrying values.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: OVERVIEW

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We create platforms and tools, powered by AI, that deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Highlights from the third quarter of fiscal year 2026 compared with the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 included:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 29% to $54.5 billion.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 99% to $627 billion.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue increased 19%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue increased 33%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: LinkedIn revenue increased 12%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Dynamics 365 revenue increased 22%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 40%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 2%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Xbox content and services revenue decreased 5%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Search advertising (formerly Search and news advertising) revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 12%.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: Our industry is dynamic and highly competitive, with frequent changes in both technologies and business models.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: Each industry shift is an opportunity to conceive new products, new technologies, or new ideas that can further transform the industry and our business.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: At Microsoft, we push the boundaries of what is possible through a broad range of research and development activities that seek to identify and address the changing demands of customers and users, industry trends, and competitive forces.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: We have a long-term strategic partnership with OpenAI which was originally established in 2019.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: In October 2025 and April 2026, we extended this partnership and continue to build on our shared vision to advance artificial intelligence responsibly and make its benefits broadly accessible.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: Microsoft is a major investor in OpenAI and will continue to receive revenue-sharing payments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Trends and Opportunities
text: We hold rights to OpenAI’s intellectual property, including models and infrastructure, for integration into our products.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The markets for software, devices, and cloud-based services are dynamic and highly competitive.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our competitors are developing new software and devices, while also deploying competing cloud-based services for consumers and businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The devices and form factors customers prefer evolve rapidly, influencing how users access services in the cloud and, in some cases, the user’s choice of which suite of cloud-based services to use.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Aggregate demand for our software, services, and devices is also correlated to global macroeconomic and geopolitical factors, which remain dynamic.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We must continue to evolve and adapt over an extended time in pace with this changing environment.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We continue to identify and evaluate opportunities to expand our datacenter locations and increase our server capacity to meet the evolving needs of our customers, particularly given the growing demand for AI services.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including graphics processing units and other components.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our devices are primarily manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: For the majority of our products, we have the ability to use other manufacturers if a current vendor becomes unavailable or unable to meet our requirements.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: However, some of our products contain certain components for which there are very few qualified suppliers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Extended disruptions at these suppliers could impact our ability to manufacture devices on time to meet consumer demand.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our success is highly dependent on our ability to attract and retain qualified employees.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We hire a mix of university and industry talent worldwide.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We compete for talented individuals globally by offering an exceptional working environment, broad customer reach, scale in resources, the ability to grow one’s career across many different products and businesses, and competitive compensation and benefits.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our international operations provide a significant portion of our total revenue and expenses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Many of these revenue and expenses are denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: As a result, changes in foreign exchange rates may significantly affect revenue and expenses.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Fluctuations in the U.S. dollar relative to certain foreign currencies increased reported revenue and expenses from our international operations for the three and nine months ended March 31, 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Further, global, regional, and local economic developments and changes in global trade policies such as restrictions on international trade, including tariffs and other controls on imports or exports, could result in increased supply chain challenges, cost volatility, and consumer and economic uncertainty which may adversely affect our results of operations.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Refer to Risk Factors (Part II, Item 1A of this Form 10-Q) for a discussion of these factors and other risks.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions
text: We remain under audit by the IRS for tax years 2014 to 2017.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions
text: With respect to the audit for tax years 2004 to 2013, on September 26, 2023, we received Notices of Proposed Adjustment (“NOPAs”) from the IRS.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions
text: The primary issues in the NOPAs relate to intercompany transfer pricing.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Uncertain Tax Positions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Valuation

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: In general, and where applicable, we use quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities to determine the fair value of our financial instruments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: This pricing methodology applies to our Level 1 investments, such as U.S. government securities, common and preferred stock, and mutual funds.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: If quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities are not available to determine fair value, then we use quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: This pricing methodology applies to our Level 2 investments, such as commercial paper, certificates of deposit, U.S. agency securities, foreign government bonds, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, corporate notes and bonds, and municipal securities.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Level 3 investments are valued using internally-developed models with unobservable inputs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis using unobservable inputs are an immaterial portion of our portfolio.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: A majority of our investments are priced by pricing vendors and are generally Level 1 or Level 2 investments as these vendors either provide a quoted market price in an active market or use observable inputs for their pricing without applying significant adjustments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Broker pricing is used mainly when a quoted price is not available, the investment is not priced by our pricing vendors, or when a broker price is more reflective of fair values in the market in which the investment trades.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Our broker-priced investments are generally classified as Level 2 investments because the broker prices these investments based on similar assets without applying significant adjustments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: In addition, all our broker-priced investments have a sufficient level of trading volume to demonstrate that the fair values used are appropriate for these investments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: Our fair value processes include controls that are designed to ensure appropriate fair values are recorded.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Valuation
text: These controls include model validation, review of key model inputs, analysis of period-over-period fluctuations, and independent recalculation of prices where appropriate.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Revenue Recognition

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Our contracts with customers often include promises to transfer multiple products and services to a customer.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Determining whether products and services are considered distinct performance obligations that should be accounted for separately versus together may require significant judgment.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: When a cloud-based service includes both on-premises software licenses and cloud services, judgment is required to determine whether the software license is considered distinct and accounted for separately, or not distinct and accounted for together with the cloud service and recognized over time.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Certain cloud services, primarily Office 365, depend on a significant level of integration, interdependency, and interrelation between the desktop applications and cloud services, and are accounted for together as one performance obligation.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Revenue from Office 365 is recognized ratably over the period in which the cloud services are provided.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Judgment is required to determine the standalone selling price (“SSP") for each distinct performance obligation.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: We use a single amount to estimate SSP for items that are not sold separately, including on-premises licenses sold with SA or software updates provided at no additional charge.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: We use a range of amounts to estimate SSP when we sell each of the products and services separately and need to determine whether there is a discount to be allocated based on the relative SSP of the various products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: In instances where SSP is not directly observable, such as when we do not sell the product or service separately, we determine the SSP using information that may include market conditions and other observable inputs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: We typically have more than one SSP for individual products and services due to the stratification of those products and services by customers and circumstances.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: In these instances, we may use information such as the size of the customer and geographic region in determining the SSP.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Due to the various benefits from and the nature of our SA program, judgment is required to assess the pattern of delivery, including the exercise pattern of certain benefits across our portfolio of customers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Our products are generally sold with a right of return, we may provide other credits or incentives, and in certain instances we estimate customer usage of our products and services, which are accounted for as variable consideration when determining the amount of revenue to recognize.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Returns and credits are estimated at contract inception and updated at the end of each reporting period if additional information becomes available.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Changes to our estimated variable consideration were not material for the periods presented.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Remaining performance obligations represent the revenue we expect to recognize for our products and services for which control has not yet been transferred to customers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: We estimate total consideration to be received at the outset of the agreement and throughout the term of the agreement.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: Estimating the total consideration and revenue that will be allocated to remaining performance obligation can involve significant judgments, including identifying and assessing variable consideration and potential renegotiation of commitments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Revenue Recognition
text: We consider factors such as the nature of the terms and duration of the contract across our portfolio of contracts.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Impairment of Investment Securities

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We review debt investments quarterly for credit losses and impairment.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If the cost of an investment exceeds its fair value, we evaluate, among other factors, general market conditions, credit quality of debt instrument issuers, and the extent to which the fair value is less than cost.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: This determination requires significant judgment.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: In making this judgment, we employ a systematic methodology that considers available quantitative and qualitative evidence in evaluating potential impairment of our investments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: In addition, we consider specific adverse conditions related to the financial health of, and business outlook for, the investee.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If we have plans to sell the security or it is more likely than not that we will be required to sell the security before recovery, then a decline in fair value below cost is recorded as an impairment charge in other income (expense), net and a new cost basis in the investment is established.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If market, industry, and/or investee conditions deteriorate, we may incur future impairments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Equity investments without readily determinable fair values are written down to fair value if a qualitative assessment indicates that the investment is impaired and the fair value of the investment is less than carrying value.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We perform a qualitative assessment on a periodic basis.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We are required to estimate the fair value of the investment to determine the amount of the impairment loss.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Once an investment is determined to be impaired, an impairment charge is recorded in other income (expense), net.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: We allocate goodwill to reporting units based on the reporting unit expected to benefit from the business combination.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: We evaluate our reporting units on an annual basis and, if necessary, reassign goodwill using a relative fair value allocation approach.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level (operating segment or one level below an operating segment) on an annual basis (May 1) and between annual tests if an event occurs or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying value.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: These events or circumstances could include a significant change in the business climate, legal factors, operating performance indicators, competition, or sale or disposition of a significant portion of a reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: Application of the goodwill impairment test requires judgment, including the identification of reporting units, assignment of assets and liabilities to reporting units, assignment of goodwill to reporting units, and determination of the fair value of each reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: The fair value of each reporting unit is estimated primarily through the use of a discounted cash flow methodology.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: This analysis requires significant judgments, including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the long-term rate of growth for our business, estimation of the useful life over which cash flows will occur, and determination of our weighted average cost of capital.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: The estimates used to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit change from year to year based on operating results, market conditions, and other factors.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Goodwill
text: Changes in these estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and goodwill impairment for each reporting unit.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: Research and Development Costs

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: Costs incurred internally in researching and developing a software product to be marketed or sold to external users are charged to expense until technological feasibility has been established for the product.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: Once technological feasibility is established, software costs are capitalized until the product is available for general release to customers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: Judgment is required in determining when technological feasibility of a product is established.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: We have determined that technological feasibility for our software products is reached after all high-risk development issues have been resolved through coding and testing.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: Generally, this occurs shortly before the products are released to production.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Research and Development Costs
text: The amortization of these costs is included in cost of revenue over the estimated life of the products.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: Legal and Other Contingencies

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: The outcomes of legal proceedings and claims brought against us are subject to significant uncertainty.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: An estimated loss from a loss contingency such as a legal proceeding or claim is accrued by a charge to income if it is probable that an asset has been impaired or a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: In determining whether a loss should be accrued we evaluate, among other factors, the degree of probability of an unfavorable outcome and the ability to make a reasonable estimate of the amount of loss.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: Changes in these factors could materially impact our consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: Income Taxes

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: The objectives of accounting for income taxes are to recognize the amount of taxes payable or refundable for the current year, and deferred tax liabilities and assets for the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in an entity’s financial statements or tax returns.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: We recognize the tax benefit from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: The tax benefits recognized in the financial statements from such a position are measured based on the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: Accounting literature also provides guidance on derecognition of income tax assets and liabilities, classification of deferred income tax assets and liabilities, accounting for interest and penalties associated with tax positions, and income tax disclosures.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: Judgment is required in assessing the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements or tax returns.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Income Taxes
text: Variations in the actual outcome of these future tax consequences could materially impact our consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part II Item 1A > GENERAL RISKS
category: GENERAL RISKS

section_path: Part I Item 1
text: ITEM 1. BUSINESS

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: GENERAL

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: Our mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: We develop and support a broad portfolio of technology solutions for individuals and businesses, focusing on secure, trusted, and innovative platforms and applications that meet evolving customer needs across AI, cloud computing, productivity and collaboration, and personal computing.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: We strive to create opportunity, growth, and impact in every country around the world.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: AI is fundamentally transforming productivity for every individual, organization, and industry.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: Microsoft's AI offerings span every layer of the technology stack, enabling transformative outcomes across sectors and unlocking opportunity for every country, community, and individual.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GENERAL
text: We believe AI should be as empowering as it is powerful, and we’re committed to designing and deploying AI responsibly with safety and security from the outset.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: What We Offer

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: Founded in 1975, we develop and support software, services, devices, and solutions that deliver new value for customers and help people and businesses realize their full potential.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: We offer an array of services, including cloud-based solutions that provide customers with AI, software, services, platforms, and content, and we provide solution support and consulting services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: We also deliver relevant online advertising to a global audience.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: Our products include operating systems, server applications, business solution applications, software development tools, desktop and server management tools, and video games.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: We also design and sell devices, including PCs, tablets, gaming and entertainment consoles, other intelligent devices, and related accessories.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: Digital transformation and adoption of AI continues to revolutionize more business workstreams for organizations in every sector across the globe.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: For enterprises, digital technology empowers employees, optimizes operations, engages customers, and in some cases, changes the very core of products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: The Microsoft Cloud provides integration across the technology stack while offering openness, improving time to value, reducing costs, and increasing agility.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: Our cloud business benefits from three economies of scale: datacenters that deploy computational resources at significantly lower cost per unit than smaller ones; datacenters that coordinate and aggregate diverse customer, geographic, and application demand patterns, improving the utilization of computing, storage, and network resources; and multi-tenancy locations that lower application maintenance labor costs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > What We Offer
text: We prioritize security above all else and we offer our customers integrated AI-driven products addressing security, compliance, identity, management, and privacy across customers’ multi-cloud, application, and device assets.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > The Ambitions That Drive Us
text: The Ambitions That Drive Us

section_path: Part I Item 1 > The Ambitions That Drive Us
text: To achieve our vision, our research and development efforts focus on three interconnected ambitions:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > The Ambitions That Drive Us
text: Reinvent productivity and business processes to help organizations and individuals work and collaborate more securely and efficiently.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > The Ambitions That Drive Us
text: Build the intelligent cloud and intelligent edge platform to provide a foundation for our customers’ digital workloads, including hybrid consistency, developer productivity, data and AI capabilities, and trusted security and compliance.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > The Ambitions That Drive Us
text: Create more personal computing experiences that empower people to play, create, and interact with technology in more intuitive, engaging, and dynamic ways.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Our Future Opportunity

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: We are focused on helping customers use the breadth and depth of the Microsoft Cloud to get the most value out of their digital spend while leading the AI platform wave across our solution areas.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: We continue to develop complete, intelligent solutions for our customers that empower people to be productive and collaborate, while safeguarding businesses and simplifying IT management.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Our goal is to lead the industry in several distinct areas of technology over the long term, which we expect will translate to sustained growth.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: We are investing significant resources in:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Tackling security from all angles with our integrated, end-to-end solutions spanning security, compliance, identity, and management, across all clouds and platforms.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Transforming the workplace to deliver new, modern, modular business applications, drive deeper insights, and improve how people communicate, collaborate, learn, work, and interact with one another.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Building and running cloud-based services in ways that utilize ubiquitous computing to unleash new experiences and opportunities for businesses and individuals.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Applying AI and ambient intelligence to drive insights, revolutionize many types of work and business processes, and provide substantive productivity gains using Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Helping customers drive frontier transformation by applying frontier AI capabilities, engineering expertise, and trusted platforms to reinvent how their organizations operate, improve decision-making, create new value, and deliver measurable business outcomes from AI.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Providing a unified intelligence layer for enterprise AI to ground AI in a continuously evolving understanding of an organization’s data.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Providing training on generative AI and greater access to digital learning and resources through skilling programs and initiatives, grants, and LinkedIn learning pathways.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Inventing new gaming experiences that bring people together around their shared love for games on any device and pushing the boundaries of innovation with console and PC gaming.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Leveraging Windows to fuel our cloud business, grow our share of the PC market, and drive increased engagement with our services like Microsoft Edge, Bing, Copilot, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Consumer, XBOX Game Pass, and more.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Our Future Opportunity
text: Our future growth depends on our ability to transcend current product category definitions, business models, and sales motions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Commitment to Sustainability
text: Commitment to Sustainability

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Commitment to Sustainability
text: Microsoft is committed to sustainability and our approach to addressing climate change starts with the sustainability of our own business.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Commitment to Sustainability
text: In 2020, we announced goals to become a carbon negative, water positive, and zero waste company by 2030.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Commitment to Sustainability
text: Since announcing these goals, we have seen major changes in both the technology sector and in our understanding of what it will take to meet our goals.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Commitment to Sustainability
text: More information about our progress toward these goals can be found in our annual Environmental Sustainability Report.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: OPERATING SEGMENTS

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: We operate our business and report our financial performance using three segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: Our segments provide management with a comprehensive financial view of our key businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: The segments enable the alignment of strategies and objectives across the development, sales, marketing, and services organizations, and they provide a framework for timely and rational allocation of resources within businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: Additional information on our operating segments and geographic and product information is contained in Note 18 – Segment Information and Geographic Data of the Notes to Financial Statements (Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K).

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATING SEGMENTS
text: Our reportable segments are described below.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: Productivity and Business Processes

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: Our Productivity and Business Processes segment consists of products and services in our portfolio of productivity, communication, and information services, spanning a variety of devices and platforms.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: This segment primarily comprises:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services, including Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, comprising Microsoft 365 Commercial, Enterprise Mobility + Security, the cloud portion of Windows Commercial, the per-user portion of Power BI, Exchange, SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Security and Compliance, and Microsoft 365 Copilot; and Microsoft 365 Commercial products, comprising Windows Commercial on-premises and Office licensed on-premises.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer products and cloud services, including Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriptions, Office licensed on-premises, and other consumer services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: LinkedIn, including Talent Solutions, Marketing Solutions, Premium Subscriptions, and Sales Solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Productivity and Business Processes
text: Dynamics products and cloud services, including Dynamics 365, comprising a set of intelligent, cloud-based applications across ERP, CRM, Power Apps, and Power Automate; and on-premises ERP and CRM applications.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services

subheading: Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial is an AI-powered business and productivity solutions platform that brings together Office, Windows, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Enterprise Mobility + Security to help organizations empower their employees.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
text: Growth depends on our ability to reach new users in new markets such as frontline workers, small and medium businesses, and growth markets, as well as add AI-enabled tools, features, and agentic scenarios to our core product and service offerings across communication, collaboration, analytics, security, compliance, and other AI business productivity categories.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Commercial Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial revenue is mainly affected by a combination of continued installed base growth and average revenue per user expansion, as well as the continued shift from Office licensed on-premises to Microsoft 365.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer is designed to increase personal productivity and creativity through a range of products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
text: Growth depends on our ability to reach new users, add value to our core product set with new features including AI tools, and continue to expand our product and service offerings into new markets.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
subheading: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue and Office Consumer products revenue is mainly affected by the percentage of customers that buy Office with their new devices and the continued shift from Office licensed on-premises to Microsoft 365 Consumer subscriptions.
