subheading: Microsoft 365 Consumer Products and Cloud Services
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue is also affected by the demand for communication and storage through Outlook.com and OneDrive, which is largely driven by subscriptions and advertising.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LinkedIn
text: LinkedIn

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LinkedIn
text: LinkedIn connects the world’s professionals to make them more productive and successful and transforms the way companies hire, market, sell, and learn.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LinkedIn
text: In addition to LinkedIn’s free services, LinkedIn offers monetized solutions designed to offer AI-enabled insights and productivity: Talent Solutions, Marketing Solutions, Premium Subscriptions, and Sales Solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LinkedIn
text: Growth will depend on our ability to increase LinkedIn member engagement on the platform and our ability to continue offering insight and AI-enabled services that provide value for our members and customers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LinkedIn
text: LinkedIn revenue is mainly affected by demand from enterprises and professionals for subscriptions to Talent Solutions, Sales Solutions, and Premium Subscriptions offerings, as well as member engagement and the quality of the sponsored content delivered to those members to drive Marketing Solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Dynamics Products and Cloud Services
text: Dynamics Products and Cloud Services

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Dynamics Products and Cloud Services
text: Dynamics provides cloud-based and on-premises business solutions for financial management, enterprise resource planning (“ERP”), customer relationship management (“CRM”), and supply chain management, as well as agentic AI and other low code application development platforms, for small and medium businesses, large organizations, and divisions of global enterprises.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Dynamics Products and Cloud Services
text: Dynamics revenue is driven by the number of users licensed and applications consumed, expansion of average revenue per user, and the continued shift to Dynamics 365, a unified set of cloud-based intelligent business applications, including our low code development platforms, such as Power Apps and Power Automate.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competitors to Office include software and global application vendors, web-based and mobile application companies, AI-first application companies, as well as local application developers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We compete by providing secure, integrated industry-specific, and easy-to-use productivity and collaboration tools and services that create comprehensive solutions and work well with technologies our customers already have both on-premises or in the cloud.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Windows faces competition from various software products and from alternative platforms and devices.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint competes with endpoint security solution providers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our Enterprise Mobility + Security offerings compete with products from a range of competitors including identity vendors, security solution vendors, and numerous other security point solution vendors.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: LinkedIn faces competition from online professional networks; recruiting, talent management, and human resource services companies; job boards; companies that provide learning and development products and services; online and offline outlets that generate revenue from advertisers and marketers; and online and offline outlets for companies with lead generation and customer intelligence and insights.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Dynamics competes with cloud-based and on-premises business solution providers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intelligent Cloud
text: Intelligent Cloud

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intelligent Cloud
text: Our Intelligent Cloud segment consists of our public, private, and hybrid server products and cloud services that power modern business and developers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intelligent Cloud
text: This segment primarily comprises:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intelligent Cloud
text: Server products and cloud services, including Azure and other cloud services, comprising cloud and AI consumption-based services, GitHub cloud services, Health and Life Sciences cloud services (formerly Nuance Healthcare cloud services), virtual desktop offerings, and other cloud services; and Server products, comprising SQL Server, Windows Server, Visual Studio, System Center, related Client Access Licenses (“CALs”), and other on-premises offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intelligent Cloud
text: Enterprise and partner services, including Enterprise Support Services, Industry Solutions, Microsoft Partner Network, and Learning Experience.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Server Products and Cloud Services

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Azure is a comprehensive set of cloud services that offer developers, IT professionals, and enterprises freedom to build, deploy, and manage applications on any platform or device.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Customers can use Azure through our global network of datacenters for computing, networking, storage, mobile and web application services, AI, and Internet of Things.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Azure enables customers to devote more resources to development and use of applications that benefit their organizations, rather than managing on-premises hardware and software.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Azure revenue is mainly affected by infrastructure-as-a-service and platform-as-a-service consumption-based services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Azure AI offerings provide a competitive advantage as companies seek ways to optimize and scale their business with AI.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: We offer supercomputing power for AI at scale to run large workloads, complemented by our rapidly expanding portfolio of AI cloud services (including the latest models) and hardware, which includes custom-built silicon and strong partnerships with chip manufacturers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Azure AI Foundry is a unified platform for developers to design, customize, and manage AI applications and agents.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Our server products are designed to make IT professionals, developers, and their systems more productive and efficient.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Server software is integrated server infrastructure and middleware designed to support software applications built on the Windows Server operating system.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: This includes the server platform, database, business intelligence, storage, management and operations, virtualization, service-oriented architecture platform, security, and identity software.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: We also license standalone and software development lifecycle tools for software architects, developers, testers, and project managers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Server products revenue is mainly affected by purchases through volume licensing programs, licenses sold to OEMs, and retail packaged products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: CALs provide access rights to certain server products, including SQL Server and Windows Server, and revenue is reported along with the associated server product.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: GitHub includes both cloud and on-premises offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: GitHub provides a collaboration platform for developers to manage code and incorporate AI and agent-based tools across the software development lifecycle.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Server Products and Cloud Services
text: Health and Life Sciences cloud services provides AI solutions to the healthcare industry.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Enterprise and Partner Services
text: Enterprise and Partner Services

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Enterprise and Partner Services
text: Enterprise and partner services assist customers in developing, deploying, and managing Microsoft server solutions, Microsoft desktop solutions, and conversational AI and ambient intelligent solutions, along with providing training and certification to developers and IT professionals on various Microsoft products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Azure faces diverse competition from cloud service providers and open-source offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Azure’s competitive advantage includes enabling a hybrid cloud, allowing deployment of existing datacenters with our public cloud into a single, cohesive infrastructure, and the ability to run at a scale that meets the needs of businesses of all sizes and complexities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers, as well as products from other emerging competitors and other open-source offerings, many of which are also current or potential partners.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our Azure Security offerings include our cloud security solution and our security information and event management solution, which compete with providers in the cybersecurity and cloud security space.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe our cloud’s global scale, coupled with our broad portfolio of identity and security solutions, allows us to effectively solve complex cybersecurity challenges for our customers and differentiates us from the competition.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our server products face competition from a wide variety of server operating systems and applications offered by companies with a range of market approaches.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Vertically integrated computer manufacturers offer their own versions of the Unix operating system preinstalled on server hardware and nearly all computer manufacturers offer server hardware for the Linux operating system.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We compete to provide enterprise-wide computing and point solutions with numerous commercial software vendors that offer solutions and middleware technology platforms, software applications for connectivity, security, hosting, database, and e-business servers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our database, business intelligence, and data warehousing solutions offerings compete with products from providers in the data and analytics industry.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our system management solutions compete with server management and server virtualization platform providers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our products for software developers compete against offerings from major technology providers, as well as open-source alternatives.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe our server products provide customers with advantages in performance, total costs of ownership, and productivity by delivering superior applications, development tools, compatibility with a broad base of hardware and software applications, security, and manageability.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our Enterprise and partner services business competes with a wide range of companies that provide strategy and business planning, application development, and infrastructure services, including multinational consulting firms and small niche businesses focused on specific technologies.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: More Personal Computing

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: Our More Personal Computing segment consists of products and services that put customers at the center of the experience with our technology.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: This segment primarily comprises:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: Windows and Devices, including Windows OEM licensing (Windows Pro and non-Pro licenses sold through the OEM channel) and Devices, comprising Surface and PC accessories.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: XBOX (formerly Gaming), including XBOX hardware and XBOX content and services, comprising first- and third-party content (including games and in-game content), XBOX Game Pass and other subscriptions, XBOX Cloud Gaming, advertising, and other cloud services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > More Personal Computing
text: Search advertising (formerly Search and news advertising), comprising Bing, Copilot, Microsoft News, Microsoft Edge, and third-party affiliates.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Windows and Devices

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: The Windows operating system is designed to deliver a more personal computing experience for users by enabling consistency of experience, applications, and information across their devices.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Windows OEM revenue is impacted significantly by the number of Windows operating system licenses purchased by OEMs, which they pre-install on the devices they sell.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: In addition to computing device market volume, Windows OEM revenue is impacted by:

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: The mix of computing devices based on form factor and screen size.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Differences in device market demand between developed markets and growth markets.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Growth of the AI PC category.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Attachment of Windows to devices shipped.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Customer mix between consumer, small and medium businesses, and large enterprises.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Changes in inventory levels in the OEM channel.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Pricing changes and promotions, pricing variation that occurs when the mix of devices manufactured shifts from local and regional system builders to large multinational OEMs, and different pricing of Windows versions licensed.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Constraints in the supply chain of device components.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Piracy.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: We design and sell devices, such as Surface (including Copilot+ PCs) and PC accessories.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Our devices are designed to enable people and organizations to connect to the people and content that matter most using Windows and integrated Microsoft products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Surface is designed to help organizations, students, and consumers be more productive.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Windows and Devices
text: Growth in Devices is dependent on total PC shipments, the ability to attract new customers, our product roadmap, and expanding into new categories.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: XBOX

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: Microsoft is expanding how billions of people globally access and play video games on PC, console, mobile, and cloud.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: Our game content is developed through a collection of first-party studios creating iconic and differentiated gaming experiences.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: We continue to invest in gaming studios and content to expand our intellectual property roadmap and leverage new content creators.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: These unique gaming experiences are the cornerstone of XBOX Game Pass, a subscription service and gaming community with access to a curated library of first- and third-party titles.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: The gamer remains at the heart of the XBOX ecosystem.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: We are identifying new opportunities to attract gamers across a variety of different end points through our first- and third-party content and business diversification across subscriptions, ads, and digital stores.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: We’ve seen new devices from third-party manufacturers along with key PC and mobile end points that help us empower gamers to play in a way that is most convenient to them.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: We are focused on growing the platform and expanding to new ecosystems to engage as many gamers as possible.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: XBOX enables people to connect and share online gaming experiences that are accessible on XBOX consoles, Windows-enabled devices, and other devices.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: XBOX is designed to benefit users by providing access to a network of certified applications and services and to benefit our developer and partner ecosystems by providing access to a large customer base.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: XBOX revenue is mainly affected by subscriptions and sales of first- and third-party content, as well as advertising.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > XBOX
text: Growth of our XBOX business is determined by the overall active user base through XBOX enabled content, availability of games, providing exclusive game content that gamers seek, the computational power and reliability of the devices used to access our content and services, and the ability to create new experiences.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: Search Advertising

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: Our Search advertising business is designed to deliver relevant search, native, and display advertising to a global audience.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: Microsoft Copilot is a digital companion designed to inform, entertain, and inspire.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: Our Microsoft Edge browser and Bing search engine with Copilot are key tools to enable user acquisition and engagement, while our technology platform enables accelerated delivery of digital advertising solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: In addition to first-party tools, we have several partnerships with companies through which we provide and monetize search offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Search Advertising
text: Growth depends on our ability to attract new users, understand intent, and match intent with relevant content on advertising offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Windows faces competition from various software products and from alternative platforms and devices.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe Windows competes effectively by giving customers choice, value, flexibility, security, an easy-to-use interface, and compatibility with a broad range of hardware and software applications, including those that enable productivity.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Devices face competition from various computer, tablet, and hardware manufacturers who offer a unique combination of high-quality industrial design and innovative technologies across various price points.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Many of these manufacturers are also current or potential partners and customers, including our Windows OEMs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: XBOX and our cloud gaming services face competition from various online gaming ecosystems and game streaming services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our gaming platform competes with other console platforms.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe our gaming platform is effectively positioned against, and uniquely differentiated from, competitive products and services based on significant innovation in hardware architecture, user interface, developer tools, online gaming and entertainment services, and continued strong content from our own first-party game franchises as well as other digital content offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our Search advertising business competes with search engines, and a wide array of websites, social platforms, and portals that provide content and online offerings to end users.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: As of June 30, 2026, we employed approximately 223,000 people on a full-time basis, 121,000 in the U.S. and 102,000 internationally.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: Of the total employees, 89,000 were in operations, including product support and consulting services, datacenter operations, and manufacturing and distribution; 77,000 were in product research and development; 43,000 were in sales and marketing; and 14,000 were in general and administration.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: Certain employees are subject to collective bargaining agreements.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: We design our programs to attract, reward, and retain top talent while fostering continuous employee development and reinforcing our organizational culture and values.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: Our total compensation offering is both highly differentiated and competitive within the market, and we also monitor pay equity across multiple dimensions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: We have invested significantly in employee wellbeing and offer a differentiated benefits package which includes many physical, emotional, and financial wellness programs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: We also provide access to continuous learning through a wide range of internal and external content, supporting professional growth across roles and disciplines.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: Through our employee listening systems, we gather direct feedback from our workforce, enabling us to adapt our programs and address employee needs globally with real-time insights.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > HUMAN CAPITAL RESOURCES
text: Additionally, our culture prioritizes the security of both our customers and Microsoft, embedding this responsibility across all teams and functions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: OPERATIONS

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: We have a global operations service center covering the Americas, Asia Pacific, Europe, and the Middle East that supports our business operations, including customer contract and order processing, billing, credit and collections, customer lifecycle AI and cloud operations, and vendor management and logistics.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: In addition to our operations center, we also operate datacenters throughout each of these regions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: We continue to align our datacenter locations and server capacity to meet the evolving needs of our customers, particularly given the growing demand for AI services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: Our datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including graphics processing units and other components.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: We engage third-party manufacturers to produce our devices and have implemented measures to enhance supply chain efficiency and resilience, including the ability to relocate production geographically.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: There are few qualified suppliers for certain components of our servers and devices.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > OPERATIONS
text: Extended or unforeseen disruptions, or limited availability of components from these suppliers could impact our ability to operate our datacenters and manufacture devices on time to meet consumer demand.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT
text: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: Product and Service Development

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: Our success is based on our ability to create new and compelling products, services, and experiences for our users, initiate and embrace disruptive technology trends, enter new geographic and product markets, and drive broad adoption of our products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: We make significant investments in research and development for new and existing products, services, and technologies, including tools and platforms spanning digital work and life experiences, cloud computing, AI, devices, security, and operating systems.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: We develop most of our products and services internally which allows us to maintain competitive advantages that come from product differentiation and closer technical control over our products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: It also gives us the freedom to decide which modifications and enhancements are most important and when they should be implemented.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: We strive to obtain information as early as possible about changing usage patterns and hardware advances that may affect software and hardware design.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: Before releasing new software platforms, and as we make significant modifications to existing platforms, we provide application vendors with a range of resources and guidelines for development, training, and testing.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: We plan to continue to make significant investments in a broad range of product research and development activities, including AI-based products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: We will coordinate our research and development across operating segments and leverage the results across the company, as appropriate.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Product and Service Development
text: This includes continuing to support fundamental research, which provides us with a unique perspective on future trends and contributes to our innovation.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: Intellectual Property

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: We protect our intellectual property investments in a variety of ways.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: We work actively in the U.S. and internationally to ensure the enforcement of copyright, patent, trademark, trade secret, and other protections that apply to our software and hardware products, services, business plans, and branding.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: While we employ much of our internally-developed intellectual property in our products and services, we also engage in outbound licensing of specific patented technologies that are incorporated into licensees’ products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: From time to time, we enter into broader cross-license agreements with other technology companies covering entire groups of patents.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: We may also purchase or license technology that we incorporate into our products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: At times, we make select intellectual property broadly available at no or low cost to achieve a strategic objective, such as promoting industry standards, advancing interoperability, supporting societal and/or environmental efforts, or attracting and enabling our external development community.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: Our engagement with open-source software also causes us to license our intellectual property rights broadly in certain situations.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: While it may be necessary in the future to seek or renew licenses relating to various aspects of our products and services, we believe, based upon past experience and industry practice, such licenses generally can be obtained on commercially reasonable terms.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Intellectual Property
text: We believe our continuing research and product development are not materially dependent on any single license or other agreement with a third-party relating to the development of our products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: Distribution occurs through a combination of direct and indirect channels.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: Direct sales activities serve customers ranging from large multinational enterprises and public sector organizations to small and medium-sized businesses.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: Indirect sales activities serve customers through a broad network of partners that support the sale, deployment, and management of Microsoft products and services worldwide.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: The indirect channel extends the reach of commercial offerings and supports customers across industries, geographies, and organization sizes.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: Sales and distribution models continue to evolve to support cloud-based, subscription-based, and consumption-based offerings while maintaining multiple options through which customers may acquire and manage our products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: OEMs license and preinstall certain Microsoft software on devices that are sold to end customers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > DISTRIBUTION, SALES, AND MARKETING
text: In addition, certain products and services are available through online purchasing channels and digital marketplaces.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LICENSING OPTIONS
text: LICENSING OPTIONS

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LICENSING OPTIONS
text: We offer a range of volume purchasing programs that enable organizations of varying sizes to acquire software, cloud services, and related support benefits through direct and partner-assisted purchasing arrangements.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > LICENSING OPTIONS
text: These programs provide customers with flexible purchasing, deployment, and management options and are tailored to large enterprises, mid-sized organizations, small businesses, educational institutions, and government entities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: GOVERNMENT REGULATION

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: We are subject to a wide range of laws, regulations, and legal requirements in the U.S. and globally, including those that may apply to our products, services, and infrastructure, and those that impose requirements related to user privacy, telecommunications, data storage and protection, advertising, and online content.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: These requirements are continually evolving, and they can be unclear and vary significantly across jurisdictions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: We have implemented comprehensive compliance programs across our operations to adapt to these changes and to maintain customer and regulator confidence.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: We monitor regulatory developments around the world and implement policies, controls, and technical safeguards so that our operations, products, and services meet applicable legal standards.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: Our business teams, with legal support, manage the compliance programs and prepare external regulatory and commercial reporting, and our internal audit teams conduct reviews of the programs and processes.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: While we have a unified approach to regulatory compliance, some of the programs and processes are tailored to meet specific regulatory obligations, such as with the creation of independent compliance functions required by the European Union (“EU”) Digital Markets Act and the EU Digital Services Act, which oversee, monitor, and assess the company’s compliance with these acts.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > GOVERNMENT REGULATION
text: For a description of the risks we face related to regulatory matters, refer to Risk Factors (Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K).

text: ITEM 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

section_path: Part II Item 7
text: The following Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations (“MD&A”) is intended to help the reader understand the results of operations and financial condition of Microsoft Corporation.

section_path: Part II Item 7
text: MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our consolidated financial statements and the accompanying Notes to Financial Statements (Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K).

section_path: Part II Item 7
text: This section generally discusses the results of our operations for the year ended June 30, 2026 compared to the year ended June 30, 2025.

section_path: Part II Item 7
text: For a discussion of the year ended June 30, 2025 compared to the year ended June 30, 2024, please refer to Part II, Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended June 30, 2025.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: OVERVIEW

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft is a technology company committed to making digital technology and artificial intelligence (“AI”) available broadly and doing so responsibly, with a mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: We create platforms and applications, powered by AI, that deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: We generate revenue by offering a wide range of cloud-based solutions, content, and other services to people and businesses; licensing and supporting an array of software products; delivering relevant online advertising to a global audience; and designing and selling devices.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Our most significant expenses are related to compensating employees; supporting and investing in our cloud-based services, including datacenter operations; designing, manufacturing, marketing, and selling our other products and services; and income taxes.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Highlights from fiscal year 2026 compared with fiscal year 2025 included:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 27% to $214.4 billion.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Commercial remaining performance obligation increased 84% to $678 billion.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue increased 17%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue increased 28%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: LinkedIn revenue increased 11%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Dynamics 365 revenue increased 18%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 41%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased slightly.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: XBOX content and services revenue decreased 5%.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > OVERVIEW
text: Search advertising (formerly Search and news advertising) revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs increased 12%.

text: Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Industry Trends and Opportunities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The markets for software, devices, and cloud-based services are dynamic and highly competitive.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our competitors are developing new software and devices, while also deploying competing cloud-based services for consumers and businesses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The devices and form factors customers prefer evolve rapidly, influencing how users access services in the cloud and, in some cases, the user’s choice of which suite of cloud-based services to use.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Aggregate demand for our software, services, and devices is also correlated to global macroeconomic and geopolitical factors, which remain dynamic.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We must continue to evolve and adapt over an extended time in pace with this changing environment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: The investments we are making in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase our operating costs and may decrease our operating margins.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We continue to identify and evaluate opportunities to expand our datacenter locations and increase our server capacity to meet the evolving needs of our customers, particularly given the growing demand for AI services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our datacenters depend on the availability of permitted and buildable land, predictable energy, networking supplies, and servers, including graphics processing units and other components.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our devices are primarily manufactured by third-party contract manufacturers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: For the majority of our products, we have the ability to use other manufacturers if a current vendor becomes unavailable or unable to meet our requirements.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: However, some of our products contain certain components for which there are very few qualified suppliers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Extended or unforeseen disruptions, or limited availability of components from these suppliers could impact our ability to operate our datacenters and manufacture devices on time to meet consumer demand.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our success is highly dependent on our ability to attract and retain qualified employees.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We hire a mix of university and industry talent worldwide.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: We compete for talented individuals globally by offering an exceptional working environment, broad customer reach, scale in resources, the ability to grow one’s career across many different products and businesses, and competitive compensation and benefits.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Our international operations provide a significant portion of our total revenue and expenses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Many of these revenue and expenses are denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: As a result, changes in foreign exchange rates may significantly affect revenue and expenses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Fluctuations in the U.S. dollar relative to certain foreign currencies increased reported revenue and did not have a material impact on reported expenses from our international operations in fiscal year 2026.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Further, global, regional, and local economic developments and changes in global trade policies such as restrictions on international trade, including tariffs and other controls on imports or exports, could result in increased supply chain challenges, cost volatility, and consumer and economic uncertainty which may adversely affect our results of operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Economic Conditions, Challenges, and Risks
text: Refer to Risk Factors (Part I, Item 1A of this Form 10-K) for a discussion of these factors and other risks.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Valuation

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: In general, and where applicable, we use quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities to determine the fair value of our financial instruments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: This pricing methodology applies to our Level 1 investments, such as U.S. government securities, common and preferred stock, and mutual funds.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: If quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities are not available to determine fair value, then we use quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: This pricing methodology applies to our Level 2 investments, such as commercial paper, certificates of deposit, U.S. agency securities, foreign government bonds, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, corporate notes and bonds, and municipal securities.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Level 3 investments are valued using internally-developed models with unobservable inputs.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Assets and liabilities measured at fair value on a recurring basis using unobservable inputs are an immaterial portion of our portfolio.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: A majority of our investments are priced by pricing vendors and are generally Level 1 or Level 2 investments as these vendors either provide a quoted market price in an active market or use observable inputs for their pricing without applying significant adjustments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Broker pricing is used mainly when a quoted price is not available, the investment is not priced by our pricing vendors, or when a broker price is more reflective of fair values in the market in which the investment trades.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Our broker-priced investments are generally classified as Level 2 investments because the broker prices these investments based on similar assets without applying significant adjustments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: In addition, all our broker-priced investments have a sufficient level of trading volume to demonstrate that the fair values used are appropriate for these investments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: Our fair value processes include controls that are designed to ensure appropriate fair values are recorded.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Valuation
text: These controls include model validation, review of key model inputs, analysis of period-over-period fluctuations, and independent recalculation of prices where appropriate.

text: CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Our consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes are prepared in accordance with GAAP.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Preparing consolidated financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > CRITICAL ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES
text: Critical accounting estimates are those estimates that involve a significant level of estimation uncertainty and could have a material impact on our financial condition or results of operations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Revenue Recognition

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Our contracts with customers often include promises to transfer multiple products and services to a customer.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Determining whether products and services are considered distinct performance obligations that should be accounted for separately versus together may require significant judgment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: When a cloud-based service includes both on-premises software licenses and cloud services, judgment is required to determine whether the software license is considered distinct and accounted for separately, or not distinct and accounted for together with the cloud service and recognized over time.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Certain cloud services, primarily Office 365, depend on a significant level of integration, interdependency, and interrelation between the desktop applications and cloud services, and are accounted for together as one performance obligation.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Revenue from Office 365 is recognized ratably over the period in which the cloud services are provided.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Judgment is required to determine the standalone selling price (“SSP”) for each distinct performance obligation.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: We use a single amount to estimate SSP for items that are not sold separately, including on-premises licenses sold with SA or software updates provided at no additional charge.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: We use a range of amounts to estimate SSP when we sell each of the products and services separately and need to determine whether there is a discount to be allocated based on the relative SSP of the various products and services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: In instances where SSP is not directly observable, such as when we do not sell the product or service separately, we determine the SSP using information that may include market conditions and other observable inputs.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: We typically have more than one SSP for individual products and services due to the stratification of those products and services by customers and circumstances.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: In these instances, we may use information such as the size of the customer and geographic region in determining the SSP.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Due to the various benefits from and the nature of our SA program, judgment is required to assess the pattern of delivery, including the exercise pattern of certain benefits across our portfolio of customers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Our products are generally sold with a right of return, we may provide other credits or incentives, and in certain instances we estimate customer usage of our products and services, which are accounted for as variable consideration when determining the amount of revenue to recognize.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Returns and credits are estimated at contract inception and updated at the end of each reporting period if additional information becomes available.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Changes to our estimated variable consideration were not material for the periods presented.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Remaining performance obligations represent the revenue we expect to recognize for our products and services for which control has not yet been transferred to customers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: We estimate total consideration to be received at the outset of the agreement and throughout the term of the agreement.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Estimating the total consideration and revenue that will be allocated to remaining performance obligation can involve significant judgments, including identifying and assessing variable consideration and potential renegotiation of commitments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: We consider factors such as the nature of the terms and duration of the contract across our portfolio of contracts.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Investments purchased by Microsoft are typically accounted for as available-for-sale debt securities, equity investments with readily determinable fair values, or equity investments without readily determinable fair values measured using either the equity method when required or at cost less impairments, if any, with adjustments for observable changes in price (referred to as the measurement alternative).

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Equity method investments may be recorded on a lag of up to three months when sufficient financial information is not available in a timely manner.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: For equity method investments recorded on a lag, we recognize the impact of intervening events that have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements in the period in which they occurred.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We review debt investments quarterly for credit losses and impairment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If the cost of an investment exceeds its fair value, we evaluate, among other factors, general market conditions, credit quality of debt instrument issuers, and the extent to which the fair value is less than cost.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: This determination requires significant judgment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: In making this judgment, we employ a systematic methodology that considers available quantitative and qualitative evidence in evaluating potential impairment of our investments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: In addition, we consider specific adverse conditions related to the financial health of, and business outlook for, the investee.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If we have plans to sell the security or it is more likely than not that we will be required to sell the security before recovery, then a decline in fair value below cost is recorded as an impairment charge in other income (expense), net and a new cost basis in the investment is established.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: If market, industry, and/or investee conditions deteriorate, we may incur future impairments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: For equity investments accounted for under the measurement alternative, we evaluate whether observable changes in price have occurred in orderly transactions for identical or similar investments of the same issuer.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: This determination requires judgment in evaluating whether transactions are orderly and whether the securities are comparable, including consideration of the rights and preferences of the securities, investor composition, and other relevant facts and circumstances.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Equity investments without readily determinable fair values are written down to fair value if a qualitative assessment indicates that the investment is impaired and the fair value of the investment is less than carrying value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We perform a qualitative assessment on a periodic basis.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: We are required to estimate the fair value of the investment to determine the amount of the impairment loss.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
subheading: Measurement and Impairment of Investment Securities
text: Once an investment is determined to be impaired, an impairment charge is recorded in other income (expense), net.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: We allocate goodwill to reporting units based on the reporting unit expected to benefit from the business combination.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: We evaluate our reporting units on an annual basis and, if necessary, reassign goodwill using a relative fair value allocation approach.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level (operating segment or one level below an operating segment) on an annual basis (May 1) and between annual tests if an event occurs or circumstances change that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: These events or circumstances could include a significant change in the business climate, legal factors, operating performance indicators, competition, or sale or disposition of a significant portion of a reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Application of the goodwill impairment test requires judgment, including the identification of reporting units, assignment of assets and liabilities to reporting units, assignment of goodwill to reporting units, and determination of the fair value of each reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: The fair value of each reporting unit is estimated primarily through the use of a discounted cash flow methodology.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: This analysis requires significant judgments, including estimation of future cash flows, which is dependent on internal forecasts, estimation of the long-term rate of growth for our business, the period over which cash flows are expected to be generated, and determination of our weighted average cost of capital.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: The estimates used to calculate the fair value of a reporting unit change from year to year based on operating results, market conditions, and other factors.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill
text: Changes in these estimates and assumptions could materially affect the determination of fair value and goodwill impairment for each reporting unit.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: Research and Development Costs

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: Costs incurred internally in researching and developing a software product to be marketed or sold to external users are charged to expense until technological feasibility has been established for the product.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: Once technological feasibility is established, software costs are capitalized until the product is available for general release to customers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: Judgment is required in determining when technological feasibility of a product is established.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: We have determined that technological feasibility for our software products is reached after all high-risk development issues have been resolved through coding and testing.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: Generally, this occurs shortly before the products are released to production.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Research and Development Costs
text: The amortization of these costs is included in cost of revenue over the estimated life of the products.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: Legal and Other Contingencies

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: The outcomes of legal proceedings and claims brought against us are subject to significant uncertainty.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: An estimated loss from a loss contingency such as a legal proceeding or claim is accrued by a charge to income if it is probable that an asset has been impaired or a liability has been incurred and the amount of the loss can be reasonably estimated.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: In determining whether a loss should be accrued we evaluate, among other factors, the degree of probability of an unfavorable outcome and the ability to make a reasonable estimate of the amount of loss.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Legal and Other Contingencies
text: Changes in these factors could materially impact our consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Income Taxes

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: The objectives of accounting for income taxes are to recognize the amount of taxes payable or refundable for the current year, and deferred tax liabilities and assets for the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in an entity’s financial statements or tax returns.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: We recognize the tax benefit from an uncertain tax position only if it is more likely than not that the tax position will be sustained on examination by the taxing authorities, based on the technical merits of the position.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: The tax benefits recognized in the financial statements from such a position are measured based on the largest benefit that has a greater than 50% likelihood of being realized upon ultimate settlement.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Accounting literature also provides guidance on derecognition of income tax assets and liabilities, classification of deferred income tax assets and liabilities, accounting for interest and penalties associated with tax positions, and income tax disclosures.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Judgment is required in assessing the future tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements or tax returns.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Variations in the actual outcome of these future tax consequences could materially impact our consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Overview

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Micron Technology, Inc. is an industry leader in innovative memory and storage solutions transforming how the world uses information to enrich life for all.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: With a relentless focus on our customers, technology leadership, and manufacturing and operational excellence, Micron delivers a rich portfolio of high-performance DRAM, NAND, and NOR memory and storage products.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Every day, the innovations that our people create fuel the data economy, enabling advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and compute-intensive applications that unleash opportunities — from the data center to the intelligent edge and across the client and mobile user experience.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: We manufacture our products at wholly-owned facilities and also utilize subcontractors for certain manufacturing processes.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Our global network of manufacturing centers of excellence not only allows us to benefit from scale while streamlining processes and operations, but it also brings together some of the world’s brightest talent to work on the most advanced memory technology.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Centers of excellence bring expertise together in one location, providing an efficient support structure for end-to-end manufacturing, with quicker cycle times, in partnership with teams, such as R&D, product development, human resources, procurement, and supply chain.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: For our locations in Singapore and Taiwan, this is also a combination of bringing fabrication and back-end manufacturing together.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: We continue to make significant investments to develop proprietary product and process technology, which generally increases bit density per wafer and reduces per-bit manufacturing costs of each generation of product.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: We continue to introduce new generations of products that offer improved performance characteristics, including higher data transfer rates, advanced packaging solutions, lower power consumption, improved read/write reliability, and increased memory density.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: We face intense competition in the semiconductor memory and storage markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: To remain competitive, we must continuously develop and implement new products and technologies and decrease manufacturing costs in spite of inflationary pressures, changing technologies, rapid market changes, and regulatory uncertainty.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Overview
text: Our success is largely dependent on obtaining returns on our R&D investments, efficient utilization of our manufacturing infrastructure, development and integration of advanced product and process technologies, market acceptance of our diversified portfolio of semiconductor-based memory and storage solutions, and efficient capital spending.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: Product Technologies

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: Our product portfolio of memory and storage solutions, advanced solutions, and storage platforms is based on our high-performance semiconductor memory and storage technologies, including DRAM, NAND, and NOR.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: We sell our products through our business units into various markets in numerous forms, including components, modules, SSDs, managed NAND, multi-chip packages, and wafers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: Many of our system-level solutions combine NAND, a controller, firmware, and in some cases DRAM.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: DRAM: DRAM products are dynamic random access memory semiconductor devices with low latency that provide high-speed data retrieval with a variety of performance characteristics.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: DRAM products lose content when power is turned off (“volatile”) and are most commonly used in the data center, client PC, graphics, industrial, mobile, and automotive markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: DRAM products include High-Bandwidth Memory (“HBM”), which is a 3D stacked DRAM architecture that utilizes through-silicon via (“TSV”) connections for more efficient communication giving it the ability to achieve a higher bandwidth while consuming less power compared to other memory types.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: NAND: NAND products are non-volatile, re-writeable semiconductor storage devices that provide high-capacity, low-cost storage with a variety of performance characteristics.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: NAND is used in SSDs for the data center, client PC, consumer, and automotive markets, and in removable storage markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: Managed NAND is used in smartphones and other mobile devices, and in the consumer, automotive, and embedded markets.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: Low-density NAND is ideal for applications like automotive, surveillance, machine-to-machine, automation, printer, and home networking.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: NOR: NOR products are non-volatile, re-writable semiconductor memory devices that provide fast read speeds.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Product Technologies
text: NOR is most commonly used for reliable code storage (e.g., boot, application, operating system, and execute-in-place code in an embedded system) and for frequently changing small data storage and is ideal for automotive, industrial, and consumer applications.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Industry Conditions
text: Industry Conditions

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: Memory and Storage Demand

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: AI-driven memory and storage growth is outpacing industry supply.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: In the third quarter of 2026, we continued to benefit from substantial improvements in pricing and margins, reflecting strong demand growth, driven in large part by the continued advancement of AI.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: The AI-driven growth in the data center has accelerated demand for memory and storage at a rate greater than our ability and the industry’s ability to increase supply.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: This has led to decisions on supply allocation that may impact certain customers and end markets as the overall market demand for memory and storage exceeds overall industry supply.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Memory and Storage Demand
text: Robust overall DRAM and NAND demand and constrained supply has led to increased pricing and improved the profitability across our portfolio.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: Strategic Customer Agreements

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: The evolving industry landscape, characterized by strong long-term customer demand for memory solutions and structurally constrained supply growth, has elevated the strategic importance of memory to our customers’ product roadmaps.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: As customers increasingly seek to secure committed long-term access to advanced memory technology and committed long-term memory supply, we have experienced increased customer engagement in strategic commitments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: In the third and fourth quarters of 2026, we entered into, and expect to continue to enter into, strategic customer agreements.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: These agreements provide customers contracted supply assurance and greater pricing visibility, and provide us higher visibility and improved stability in our business performance.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: Strategic customer agreements are structured as take-or-pay agreements, with binding commitments for specific volumes over the multi-year contract terms.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: Pricing for most agreements is either fixed, or is subject to minimum and maximum pricing.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: The largest agreements generally have a ceiling price for existing products that approximates the market price in the second calendar quarter of 2026, and a floor price through the term of the agreement.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: A minority of the agreements do not have any fixed pricing or price bands, as pricing for those agreements is subject to market conditions.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: We expect gross margins from our strategic customer agreements with price bands, even at floor pricing levels, to yield gross margins well above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Strategic Customer Agreements
text: Accordingly, we believe these agreements accelerate the transformation of our business model and will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of our financial performance.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Our primary sources of liquidity are cash generated from operations and financing obtained from capital markets and financial institutions.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Cash generated from operations is highly dependent on selling prices for our products, which can vary significantly from period to period.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Cash and marketable investments totaled $30.13 billion as of May 28, 2026, and $11.94 billion as of August 28, 2025.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Our cash and investments consist primarily of bank deposits, money market funds, and liquid investment-grade, fixed-income securities, which are diversified among industries and individual issuers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: To mitigate credit risk, we invest through high-credit-quality financial institutions and by policy generally limit the concentration of credit exposure by restricting the amount of investments with any single obligor.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: As of May 28, 2026, $5.40 billion of our cash and marketable investments was held by our foreign subsidiaries.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: We recently executed certain strategic customer agreements, including agreements executed subsequent to May 28, 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: These agreements include binding commitments for specific volumes over the multi-year contract terms.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Strategic customer agreements often include substantial customer deposits and related financial commitments.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: In connection with these strategic customer agreements, we expect to receive cash deposits and related financial commitments of $22 billion for agreements concluded to date.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Approximately $18 billion of these commitments will be in the form of cash deposits.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: We continuously evaluate alternatives for efficiently funding our capital expenditures and ongoing operations.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: As of May 28, 2026, $2.00 billion was available to draw under our Revolving Credit Facility.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Funding of certain significant capital projects is also supported by the receipt of government incentives.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Our incentives are conditioned upon achieving or maintaining certain outcomes and satisfying compliance requirements and are subject to reduction, termination, or clawback.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: To develop new product and process technology, support future growth, achieve operating efficiencies, and maintain product quality, we must continue to invest in manufacturing technologies, facilities and equipment, and R&D.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: We estimate capital expenditures for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $27 billion in 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > Liquidity and Capital Resources
text: Actual amounts for 2026 will vary depending on market conditions and may vary from quarter to quarter due to the timing of expenditures and proceeds from government incentives.
