section_path: Part I Item 1 > Seasonality
text: Seasonality

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Seasonality
text: We have historically experienced a sequential decline in revenues in the first quarter of our fiscal year, as the sales organization spends time developing new business after higher close rates in the fourth quarter, and because sales to European customers are typically weaker during the summer months.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Seasonality
text: We derive a substantial amount of our revenue in any given quarter from customer orders booked in the same quarter.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Seasonality
text: Customer orders and revenues typically follow intra-quarter seasonality patterns weighted toward the end of the quarter.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Seasonality
text: As recurring services and cloud revenue increase as a percentage of our total revenues, historical seasonal patterns may become less pronounced.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: Backlog

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: We manufacture products based on a combination of specific order requirements and forecasts of our customers’ demand.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: Orders are generally placed by customers on an as-needed basis.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: A substantial portion of our products is sold on the basis of standard purchase orders that are cancelable prior to shipment without penalty.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: In certain circumstances, purchase orders are subject to change with respect to timing of fulfillment, quantity of product or timing of delivery resulting from changes in customer requirements or supply chain constraints.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: Our business is characterized by seasonal and intra-quarter variability in demand, as well as short lead times and product delivery schedules.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Backlog
text: Accordingly, backlog may vary materially quarter to quarter and at any given time may not be a meaningful indicator of future revenue.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: Manufacturing and Supply Chain

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We have outsourced manufacturing operations to third parties located in Fremont, California; San Jose, California; Laredo, Texas; Guadalajara, Mexico; Helmond, The Netherlands; Tiszaujvaros, Hungary; Taoyuan, Taiwan; and Singapore.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: These operations include materials procurement, commodity management, component engineering, test engineering, manufacturing engineering, product assembly, product assurance, quality control, final test, and global logistics.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We rely on a limited number of suppliers for materials, as well as several key subcontractors for the production of certain subassemblies and finished systems.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We strive to have multiple suppliers qualified to provide critical components where possible and have our products manufactured in a number of locations to mitigate our supply chain risk.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: Our strategy has been to develop close relationships with our suppliers, maximizing the exchange of critical information and facilitating the implementation of joint quality programs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We use contract manufacturers for the production of major subassemblies and final system configuration.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: This manufacturing strategy minimizes capital investments and overhead expenditures while creating flexibility for rapid expansion.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We are certified to the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 certification standards.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Manufacturing and Supply Chain
text: We have been Tier 2 certified under the U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s (CBP) Customs Trade Partnership Against Terrorism (CTPAT) program since January 2015 and have been a member of the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) since 2013.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Research and Development

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Our research and development (R&D) team delivers innovation to help customers make their data intelligent.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Our R&D structure supports the execution and acceleration of our strategies and roadmaps across product groups.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: We use our expertise and shared intellectual property to develop cloud services and hybrid-cloud solutions that help customers adapt to changing business imperatives.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Most of our R&D efforts are dedicated to the ongoing development and enhancement of the software that powers our solutions.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Our R&D priorities are defined by how we can help organizations realize operational simplicity, cyber resilience and security, AI innovation, and infrastructure savings and agility.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: We design our products and services with AI and cloud connectivity in mind, including our capabilities for cyber resiliency, tiering, disaster recovery, replication, bursting, and migration.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: We conduct research and development activities in various locations throughout the world.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Total research and development expenses were $991 million in fiscal 2026, $1,012 million in fiscal 2025 and $1,029 million in fiscal 2024.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: These costs consist primarily of personnel and related expenses incurred to conduct product development activities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: Although we develop many of our products internally, we also acquire technology through business combinations or through third-party licensing when appropriate.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Research and Development
text: We believe that technical leadership is essential to our success, and we expect to continue to commit substantial resources to research and development.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We operate in markets characterized by rapid technological change, evolving customer requirements, and frequent introductions of new products, services, and business models.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Customer demand continues to be influenced by cloud adoption, digital transformation initiatives, cybersecurity requirements, and increasing use of artificial intelligence and data‑driven applications.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We compete in the storage, data management, and AI data pipeline markets, including on-premises infrastructure, hybrid cloud environments, and public cloud services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our offerings compete with a wide range of vendors that provide data storage systems, data management software, and related services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Some competitors offer broad portfolios spanning multiple infrastructure and software categories, while others focus on specific technologies, workloads, or delivery models.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In hybrid and on‑premises environments, we compete against solutions that customers purchase through capital expenditures, as well as alternatives that emphasize consumption‑based or subscription models.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In public cloud environments, customers may choose native cloud services that are consumed as operating expenses.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We both partner with and compete against cloud service providers through our cloud‑based software and services offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We also compete in software-defined and cloud operations markets with solutions that address data mobility, orchestration, observability, automation, security, and application lifecycle management.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition in these areas includes established technology providers as well as newer market entrants, including startups, and offerings introduced by cloud service providers as part of their broader platforms.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: The emergence of artificial intelligence workloads has introduced additional competitive dynamics, particularly in areas related to data readiness, performance, scalability, and integration with compute and cloud ecosystems.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In these markets, competition includes both established infrastructure vendors and newer entrants focused on AI-oriented use cases and architectures.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition in our markets is intense and includes factors such as product functionality, performance, reliability, security, ease of use, integration capabilities, pricing and total cost of ownership, delivery models, and quality of customer support and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We also face competition from alternative architectures or approaches that may reduce or eliminate demand for some of our offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In addition, our current or potential competitors may form strategic alliances or partnerships among themselves or with third parties, including some of our own partners, which could increase competitive pressures.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: New competitors, technologies, or business models may also emerge.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe our enduring competitive advantage is built on a foundation of strategic differentiation and deep customer-centricity.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We will continue to lead by: • Driving Relentless Innovation: Our differentiation is rooted in our sustained commitment to hardware and software innovation, deep cloud integration, and a rich ecosystem of technology partnerships. • Delivering a Strong Customer Experience: We forge lasting relationships with our customers and partners. Our goal is to provide an outstanding experience at every touchpoint, offering a full range of expertise before, during, and after their initial purchase. This holistic approach is a cornerstone of our competitive strategy and our key to winning in the market.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: Proprietary Rights

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: We generally rely on patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret and contract laws to establish and maintain our proprietary rights in our technology, products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: While our intellectual property rights are important to our success, we believe that our business is not materially dependent on any particular patent, trademark, copyright, license or other individual intellectual property right.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: We have been granted, or own by assignment, well over two thousand U.S. patents, hundreds of pending U.S. patent applications, and many corresponding patents and patent applications in other countries.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: From time to time, we may make certain intellectual property available under an open source license.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: Our primary trademarks are NetApp and the NetApp design logo, which are registered trademarks in the U.S. and in many other countries.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: In addition, we have trademarks and trademark registrations in the U.S. and other countries covering our various product or service names.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: We generally enter into confidentiality agreements with our employees, resellers, distributors, customers, and suppliers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: In addition, through various licensing arrangements, we receive certain rights to the intellectual property of others.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: We expect to maintain current licensing arrangements and to secure additional licensing arrangements in the future, as needed and to the extent available on reasonable terms and conditions, to support continued development and sales of our products and services.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: Some of these licensing arrangements require or may require royalty payments and other licensing fees.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: The amount of these payments and fees may depend on various factors, including but not limited to the structure of royalty payments; offsetting considerations, if any; and the degree of use of the licensed technology.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: The industry in which we compete is characterized by rapidly changing technology, a large number of patents, and frequent claims and related litigation regarding intellectual property rights, and we may be exposed to various risks related to such claims or legal proceedings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Proprietary Rights
text: If we are unable to protect our intellectual property, we may be subject to increased competition that could materially and adversely affect our business operations, financial condition, results of operations and/or cash flows.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: Environmental Disclosure

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We believe that our commitment to helping our customers and partners succeed and to positively affecting the communities where our employees work and live supports our efforts to deliver value to our stockholders.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We are committed to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions; the efficient use of resources; and reducing, relative to the growth of the Company, the environmental impacts from our operations, products, and services, as well as complying with laws and regulations related to these areas.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We voluntarily measure, monitor, and publicly report our scope 1, scope 2, and scope 3 (partial) greenhouse gas emissions, waste and water impacts.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We seek to optimize the energy efficiency of our buildings, labs, and data centers; and we have increased our use of renewable energy, especially at our facilities in Bangalore, India (95% of the total energy consumed is renewable); Cork, Ireland (100% of electricity consumed is from renewable energy) and Wichita, Kansas (100% of the electricity consumed is produced by renewable wind energy).

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: At the global, regional and state levels, various laws and regulations have been implemented or are under consideration to mitigate or report on the effects of climate change and other environmental topics.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: Environmental laws are complex and have tended to become more stringent over time.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: However, it is difficult to anticipate future regulations pertaining to environmental matters and to estimate their impacts on our operations.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: Additionally, we have implemented disaster recovery and business resiliency measures to mitigate the physical risks our facilities, business, and supply chain might face as a consequence of natural disasters, earthquakes, floods, droughts, and other such occurrences or severe weather/climate-related phenomena.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We are subject to international, federal, state, and local regulations regarding workplace safety and protection of the environment.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: Various international, federal, state, and local provisions regulate the use and discharge of certain hazardous materials used in the manufacture of our products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: Failure to comply with environmental regulations in the future could cause us to incur substantial costs, subject us to business interruptions or cause customers to cease purchasing from us.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We strive to comply with all applicable environmental laws.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: All of our products meet the applicable requirements of the following European Union (EU) directives: Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH); Energy Related Products (ErP); and Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS).

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We also comply with the China RoHS directive.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We have a global product take-back program and an e-waste scheme to comply with the EU directive on Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE), and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations in India, Singapore and California.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: In addition, EPR regulations continue to expand in scope and to new jurisdictions globally, and the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), which entered into force in February 2025, will introduce additional packaging and EPR obligations beginning in August 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We maintain an environmental management system that provides the framework for setting, monitoring, and continuously improving our environmental goals and objectives.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: As part of ISO 14001 requirements, we set local environmental performance goals, such as reducing energy consumption per square foot and minimizing waste generated on site, ensuring these goals support our broader corporate strategy.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Disclosure
text: We also conduct periodic reviews and third-party audits, and we monitor environmental legislation and requirements to remain compliant with applicable laws - both in our operations and for our products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Human Capital
text: Human Capital

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Human Capital
text: We take pride in, and believe our success depends on, attracting and retaining leading talent in the industry based on a culture-fit approach.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Human Capital
text: From our inception, NetApp has worked to build a model company and has embraced a culture of openness and trust.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Human Capital
text: Our employees are encouraged to be innovative, and we communicate openly and transparently so that employees can focus on critical and impactful work that ties directly to our business strategy.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Human Capital
text: We continue to invest in our global workforce to support inclusion and belonging and our employees’ well-being and development.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Belonging
text: Belonging

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Belonging
text: We believe inclusion and belonging lead to more innovation, better access to talent and improved business outcomes.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Belonging
text: Our strategies are intended to promote a team-based culture, inclusiveness, and to achieve sustained business results.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: Our healthcare options offer competitive, comprehensive coverage for our employees and their families, including: • National medical plans; • Regional medical plans; • Expert advice from world-renowned doctors through our medical second opinion program; • National dental plans; • National vision plans; and • A robust wellness program.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: Insurance and income protection.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: We provide life, accidental death and dismemberment and disability insurance programs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: For additional peace of mind, we also offer supplemental insurance for our employees and their dependents.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: Financial and savings programs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Benefits, Wellbeing and Engagement
text: We offer flexible spending accounts, an employee stock purchase plan and competitive retirement plans, including options to maximize retirement savings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: Flexible Work.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: We take a hybrid‑first approach to work, grounded in the belief that how and where we work should support strong outcomes, meaningful collaboration, and sustained performance.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: Our flexible hybrid model gives employees, in partnership with their managers and teams, the ability to balance flexibility with intentional time together - recognizing that some roles require regular in‑person presence or are tied to specific locations based on business needs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: We use digital‑first tools and workflows to enable productivity and flexibility, wherever work happens.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: At the same time, we believe there is unique value in coming together in person - to build relationships, strengthen trust, and foster collaboration and innovation.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Flexible Work.
text: Our offices serve as hubs for connection and teamwork, creating opportunities for people to learn from one another and do their best work together.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Employee Wellbeing.
text: Employee Wellbeing.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Employee Wellbeing.
text: We provide a wide range of wellbeing programs and tools to ensure employees and their families have the resources they need when they need them.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Employee Wellbeing.
text: We offer emotional wellbeing resources and programs such as back-up child and elder care, student debt repayment, educational assistance, and legal services for employees and their dependents.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Employee Wellbeing.
text: NetApp also offers a variety of time-off programs to help support our employees who need time-off.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Employee Wellbeing.
text: Employees also have access to discounts and fitness centers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engagement.
text: Engagement.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engagement.
text: We help employees grow, develop and succeed at NetApp by encouraging an open and interactive culture, where individual needs are recognized and met, and Company goals are supported.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engagement.
text: For employees, growth goals are tied to corporate objectives and key results to ensure that employees are progressing and are supported by management teams.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engagement.
text: Managers are encouraged to set aside time at least each quarter to conduct a two-way conversation with each team member to offer feedback, guidance and support on goals, priorities and career development.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engagement.
text: The Company also conducts surveys that gauge employee sentiment in areas like cross-functional collaboration, manager performance and inclusivity and create action plans to address concerns and amplify opportunities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Giving Back.
text: Giving Back.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Giving Back.
text: The NetApp Cares programs support our employees' efforts to make a positive difference in our communities, which we believe contributes to our culture by enhancing employee engagement and team building.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Giving Back.
text: In fiscal 2026, NetApp employees donated over 28,000 hours to serve their communities and make an impact around the world.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Giving Back.
text: The NetApp Cares programs encourage employees to volunteer through individual, team or company efforts.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: George Kurian is the Chief Executive Officer of NetApp, a position he has held since June 1, 2015.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: He joined our Board of Directors in June 2015.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: From September 2013 to May 2015, he was Executive Vice President of Product Operations, overseeing all aspects of technology strategy, product and solutions development across our portfolio.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: Mr. Kurian joined NetApp in April 2011 as the Senior Vice President of the Storage Solutions group and was appointed to Senior Vice President of the Data ONTAP group in December 2011.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: Prior to joining NetApp, Mr. Kurian held several positions with Cisco Systems from 2002 to 2011, including Vice President and General Manager of the Application Networking and Switching Technology group.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: Additional roles include Vice President of Product Management and Strategy at Akamai Technologies from 1999 to 2002, as well as a management consultant at McKinsey and Company and a leader on the software engineering and product management teams at Oracle Corporation.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers
text: Mr. Kurian is a board member at Cigna Corporation, a global health services company, where he serves on the compliance committee and people resources committee, and holds a BS degree in electrical engineering from Princeton University and an MBA degree from Stanford University.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Information About Our Executive Officers

category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: Changes to any of these factors could materially impact our operating results, financial condition and cash flows.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: For example, in July 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was enacted, which introduced significant changes to U.S. tax law, including permanent extension of certain expiring provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, modifications to the international tax framework and the restoration of favorable tax treatment for certain business provisions including the immediate expensing of United States research and development expenditures.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: Many countries around the world are beginning to implement legislation and other guidance to align their international tax rules with the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Base Erosion and Profit Shifting Project (BEPS) recommendation and related action plans that aim to standardize and modernize global corporate tax policy, including changes to cross-border tax, transfer pricing documentation rules and nexus-based tax incentive practices.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: We operate in jurisdictions that participate in the BEPS inclusive framework (Inclusive Framework), which is implementing measures such as the global minimum tax framework known as Pillar Two and standardized profit requirements for baseline marketing and distribution activities under Amount B of Pillar One.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: These rules, along with the continued expansion of the Inclusive Framework to additional jurisdictions or any changes to the scope or requirements of these frameworks, could increase our worldwide effective tax rate and adversely affect our operating results, financial condition, and cash flows.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors
text: If the ultimate determination of income taxes or at-source withholding taxes assessed under these audits results in amounts in excess of the tax provision we have recorded or reserved for, our operating results, financial condition and cash flows could be adversely affected.

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors
category: General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors

section_path: Part I Item 1A > General Risk Factors

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Executive Overview
text: Executive Overview

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Our Company

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: NetApp is a global leader in Intelligent Data Infrastructure, empowering organizations to realize the full potential of their data in a rapidly evolving digital world.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Headquartered in San Jose, California, and serving customers in approximately 150 countries, NetApp delivers innovative solutions that enable seamless data management, protection, and mobility across on-premises, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Our flagship ONTAP® data management software, together with a comprehensive portfolio of all-flash, hybrid-flash, and cloud-native offerings, forms the foundation for customers’ digital transformation initiatives.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: NetApp’s deep integration with all major public cloud providers—AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud—enables our customers to run critical workloads anywhere, with consistent performance, security, and governance.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: NetApp's strategic focus is on modernizing data infrastructure, enabling resilient and secure operations, optimizing cloud strategies, and accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) adoption.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Through continued investment in innovation, we have expanded our portfolio to include advanced AI-ready infrastructure, Storage-as-a-Service (Keystone), and robust cyber resilience solutions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Our partnerships with leading technology companies and a global ecosystem of channel partners further extend our reach and solution capabilities.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Our operations are organized into two segments: Hybrid Cloud and Public Cloud.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Hybrid Cloud offers a unified data storage portfolio of storage management and infrastructure solutions that helps customers modernize their data centers.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Our Hybrid Cloud portfolio accommodates both structured and unstructured data with unified storage optimized for flash, disk, and cloud storage, capable of handling data-intensive workloads and applications.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Hybrid Cloud includes software, hardware, and related support, along with professional and other services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: Public Cloud offers a portfolio of products delivered primarily as-a-service, including related support.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: This portfolio includes cloud storage, data services, and operational services.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Our Company
text: These services are generally available on the leading public clouds, including AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Global Business Environment
text: Global Business Environment

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: Supply Chain

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: Inflationary pressures and supply chain constraints have impacted our operations beginning in the second half of fiscal 2026.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: We have experienced increased costs for memory and other components, which have affected our gross margins, and we expect costs will remain elevated, or continue to increase, in the near term.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: Additionally, the tight supply environment for specific products, which is anticipated to persist, could pose challenges in meeting customer demand for those products.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: To address these challenges, we have implemented several strategic actions:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: We raised our pricing in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, in line with market trends.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: We expect to continue adjusting prices as necessary to offset rising costs and remain aligned with the market.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain
text: While we aim to match supplier costs with our pricing to customers, we recognize the need to give customers time to adjust to these changes.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Supply Chain

text: This includes competitive storage options, all-flash solutions, hybrid-flash solutions, public cloud solutions, and our Keystone Storage-as-a-Service offering.

text: These actions are part of our ongoing efforts to mitigate the impact of inflation and supply chain constraints on our operating results.

text: Our estimates are based on historical experience and various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Critical Accounting Estimates
text: We believe that the accounting estimates employed and the resulting balances are reasonable; however, actual results may differ from these estimates and such differences may be material.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Critical Accounting Estimates
text: The summary of significant accounting policies is included in Note 1 – Description of Business and Significant Accounting Policies of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in Part II, Item 8.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Critical Accounting Estimates
text: An accounting policy is deemed to be critical if it requires an accounting estimate to be made based on assumptions about matters that are highly uncertain at the time the estimate is made, if different estimates reasonably could have been used, and if changes in the estimate that are reasonably possible could materially impact the financial statements.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Critical Accounting Estimates
text: The accounting policies described below reflect the significant judgments, estimates and assumptions used in the preparation of the consolidated financial statements.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Revenue Recognition

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Our contracts with customers often include the transfer of multiple products and services to the customer.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: In determining the amount and timing of revenue recognition, we assess which products and services are distinct performance obligations and allocate the transaction price, which may include fixed and/or variable amounts, among each performance obligation on a relative standalone selling price (SSP) basis.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: The following are the key estimates and assumptions and corresponding uncertainties included in this approach:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: | Key Estimates and Assumptions | | | Key Uncertainties |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text:  | We evaluate whether products and services promised in our contracts with customers are distinct performance obligations that should be accounted for separately versus together. | |  | In certain contracts, the determination of our distinct performance obligations requires significant judgment.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: As our business and offerings to customers change over time, the products and services we determine to be distinct performance obligations may change.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Such changes may adversely impact the amount of revenue and gross margin we report in a particular period. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text:  | In determining the transaction price of our contracts, we estimate variable consideration based on the expected value, primarily relying on our history.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: In certain situations, we may also use the most likely amount as the basis of our estimate. | |  | We may have insufficient relevant historical data or other information to arrive at an accurate estimate of variable consideration using either the “expected value” or “most likely amount” method.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Additionally, changes in business practices, such as those related to sales returns or marketing programs, |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: | | | | may introduce new forms of variable consideration, as well as more complexity and uncertainty in the estimation process. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text:  | In contracts with multiple performance obligations, we establish SSPs based on the price at which products and services are sold separately.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: If SSPs are not observable through past transactions, we estimate them by maximizing the use of observable inputs including pricing strategy, market data, internally-approved pricing guidelines related to the performance obligations and other observable inputs. | |  | As our business and offerings evolve over time, modifications to our pricing and discounting methodologies, changes in the scope and nature of product and service offerings and/or changes in customer segmentation may result in a lack of consistency, making it difficult to establish and/or maintain SSPs.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: Changes in SSPs could result in different and unanticipated allocations of revenue in contracts with multiple performance obligations.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Revenue Recognition
text: These factors, among others, may adversely impact the amount of revenue and gross margin we report in a particular period. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: We allocate the purchase price of acquisitions to identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed at their acquisition date fair values based on established valuation techniques.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: Goodwill represents the residual value as of the acquisition date, which in most cases is measured as the excess of the purchase consideration transferred over the net of the acquisition date fair values of the assets acquired and liabilities assumed.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: The carrying values of purchased intangible assets are reviewed whenever events and circumstances indicate that the net book value of an asset may not be recovered through expected future cash flows from its use and eventual disposition.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: We periodically review the estimated remaining useful lives of our intangible assets.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: This review may result in impairment charges or shortened useful lives, resulting in charges to our consolidated statements of income.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: We review goodwill for impairment annually and whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying amount of one of our reporting units may exceed its fair value.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: The provisions of the accounting standard for goodwill allow us to first assess qualitative factors to determine whether it is necessary to perform the quantitative goodwill impairment test.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: For our annual goodwill impairment test in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, we performed a qualitative assessment of goodwill impairment by evaluating relevant factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of each of our reporting units is less than their carrying values.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: As a result of the qualitative assessment, we determined the quantitative test was not necessary and there was no impairment of goodwill.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: The following are the key estimates and assumptions and corresponding uncertainties for estimating the value of our goodwill and purchased intangible assets:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: | Key Estimates and Assumptions | | | Key Uncertainties |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text:  | The assessment of fair value for goodwill and purchased intangible assets is based on factors that market participants would use in an orderly transaction in accordance with the accounting guidance for the fair value measurement of nonfinancial assets.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: The valuation of purchased intangible assets is principally based on estimates of the future performance and cash flows expected to be generated by the acquired assets from the acquired business. | |  | While we employ experts to determine the acquisition date fair value of acquired intangibles, the fair values of assets acquired and liabilities assumed are based on significant management assumptions and estimates, which are inherently uncertain and highly subjective and as a result, actual results may differ from estimates.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: If different assumptions were to be used, it could materially impact the purchase price allocation. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text:  | Evaluations of possible goodwill and purchased intangible asset impairment require us to make judgments and assumptions related to the allocation of our balance sheet and income statement amounts and estimate future cash flows and fair market values of our reporting units and assets. | |  | In response to changes in industry and market conditions, we could be required to strategically realign our resources and consider restructuring, disposing of, or otherwise exiting businesses, which could result in an impairment of goodwill or purchased intangible assets.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: Assumptions and estimates about expected future cash flows and the fair values of our reporting units and purchased intangible assets are complex and subjective.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: They can be affected by a variety of factors, including external factors such as the adverse impact of unanticipated changes in macroeconomic conditions, and technological changes or new product introductions from competitors.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: They can also be affected by internal factors such as changes in business strategy or in forecasted product life cycles and roadmaps.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Goodwill and Purchased Intangible Assets
text: Our ongoing consideration of these and other factors could result in future impairment charges or accelerated amortization expense, which could adversely affect our operating results. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Income Taxes

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: We are subject to income taxes in the United States and numerous foreign jurisdictions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: We compute our provision for income taxes using the asset and liability method, under which deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the expected future tax consequences of temporary differences between the financial reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities, and for operating losses and tax credit carryforwards.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using the currently enacted tax rates that apply to taxable income in effect for the years in which those tax assets or liabilities are expected to be realized or settled.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: The Company records a valuation allowance to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount that is believed more likely than not to be realized.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: The following are the key estimates and assumptions and corresponding uncertainties for our income taxes:

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: | Key Estimates and Assumptions | | | Key Uncertainties |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text:  | Our income tax provision is based on existing tax law and advanced pricing agreements or letter rulings we have with various tax authorities. | |  | Our provision for income taxes is subject to volatility and could be adversely impacted by future changes in existing tax laws, such as a change in tax rate, possible U.S. changes to the taxation of earnings of our foreign subsidiaries, and uncertainties as to future renewals of favorable tax agreements and rulings. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text:  | The determination of whether we should record or adjust a valuation allowance against our deferred tax assets is based on assumptions regarding our future profitability. | |  | Our future profits could differ from current expectations resulting in a change to our determination as to the amount of deferred tax assets that are more likely than not to be realized.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: We could adjust our valuation allowance with a corresponding impact to the tax provision in the period in which such determination is made. |

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text:  | The estimates for our uncertain tax positions are based primarily on company specific circumstances, applicable tax laws, tax opinions from outside firms and past results from examinations of our income tax returns. | |  | Significant judgment is required in evaluating our uncertain tax positions.

section_path: Part II Item 7 > Income Taxes
text: Although we believe our reserves are reasonable, no assurance can be given that the final tax outcome or tax court rulings of these matters will not be different from that which is reflected in our historical tax provisions and accruals. |

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: OVERVIEW

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: The Company is a global leader in motion and control technologies.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Leveraging a unique combination of interconnected technologies, we design, manufacture, and provide aftermarket support for highly engineered solutions that create value for customers primarily in aerospace and defense, in-plant and industrial equipment, transportation, off-highway, energy, and HVAC and refrigeration markets around the world.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: By aligning around our purpose, Enabling Engineering Breakthroughs that Lead to a Better Tomorrow, Parker is better positioned for the challenges and opportunities of tomorrow.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: The Win Strategy is Parker's business system that defines the goals and initiatives that create responsible, sustainable growth and enable Parker's long-term success.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: It works with our purpose, which is a foundational element of The Win Strategy, to engage team members and create responsible and sustainable growth.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Our shared values shape our culture and our interactions with stakeholders and the communities in which we operate and live.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We believe many opportunities for profitable growth are available.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: The Company intends to focus primarily on business opportunities in the areas of aerospace and defense, in-plant and industrial equipment, transportation, off-highway, energy and HVAC and refrigeration.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We believe we can meet our strategic objectives by:

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: serving the customer and continuously enhancing its experience with the Company;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: successfully executing The Win Strategy initiatives relating to engaged people, customer experience, profitable growth and financial performance;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: maintaining a decentralized division and sales company structure;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: fostering a safety-first and entrepreneurial culture;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: engineering innovative systems and products to provide superior customer value through improved service, efficiency and productivity;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: delivering products, systems and services that have demonstrable savings to customers and are priced by the value they deliver;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: enabling a sustainable future by providing innovative technology solutions that offer a positive global environmental impact and operating responsibly by reducing our energy use and emissions;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: acquiring strategic businesses;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: organizing around targeted regions, technologies and markets;

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: driving efficiency by implementing lean enterprise principles; and

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: creating a culture of empowerment through our values, inclusion, accountability and teamwork.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We manage our supply chain through our "local for local" manufacturing strategy, ongoing supplier management process and broadened supply base.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We actively monitor global trade policies and inflation, managing their impact through a variety of cost and pricing measures.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: In addition, continuous improvement and lean initiatives, along with disciplined workforce and discretionary spending management, further enhance our ability to mitigate these impacts.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: At the same time, we are appropriately addressing the ongoing needs of our business so that we continue to serve our customers.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Over the long term, the extent to which our business and results of operations will be impacted by global economic and political uncertainty and geopolitical risks depends on future developments that remain uncertain.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: In particular, the tariff environment continues to be very dynamic.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: In February 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA") on goods imported into the U.S. were unauthorized.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We will continue to monitor developments; however, given the uncertainty surrounding potential refunds, we have not recorded a receivable for IEEPA tariffs paid as of March 31, 2026.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: Additionally, geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, including the ongoing conflict involving Iran, could adversely affect global supply chains and exert upward pressure on commodity, energy and logistic costs.

section_path: Part I Item 2 > OVERVIEW
text: We will continue to monitor the global environment and manage our business with the goal to minimize unfavorable impacts on operations and financial results.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Competition

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Parker operates in highly competitive markets and industries.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We offer our products over numerous, varied markets through our divisions operating in 44 countries.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our global scope means that we have hundreds of competitors across our various markets and product offerings.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Our competitors include U.S. and non-U.S. companies.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: These competitors and the degree of competition vary widely by product lines, end markets, geographic scope and/or geographic locations.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Although each of our segments has numerous competitors, given our market and product breadth, no single competitor competes with the Company with respect to all the products we manufacture and sell.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In the Diversified Industrial Segment, Parker competes based on product quality and innovation, customer experience, manufacturing and distribution capability, aftermarket support, and price competitiveness.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe that we are one of the market leaders in most of the major markets for our most significant Diversified Industrial Segment products.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We have comprehensive motion and control technologies allowing us to provide the broadest systems capabilities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: While our primary global competitors include Bosch Rexroth AG, Copeland, Danaher Corporation, Danfoss A/S, Donaldson Company, Inc., Emerson/ASCO, Festo SE & Co., Freudenberg-NOK, Gates Corporation, IMI/Norgren, SMC Corporation, Swagelok Company, and Trelleborg AB, none of these businesses compete with every group or product in our Diversified Industrial Segment.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: In the Aerospace Systems Segment, we have developed relationships with key customers based on our advanced technological and engineering capabilities, performance in quality, delivery, service, and price competitiveness.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: This has enabled us to obtain significant original equipment business on new aircraft programs for our systems and components, as well as the follow-on repair and replacement business for these programs.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Further, the Aerospace Systems Segment utilizes design and manufacturing techniques as well as best cost region and supply chain management strategies to reduce cost.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Although we believe that we are one of the market leaders in most of the major markets for our most significant Aerospace Systems Segment products, primary global competitors for these products include Crane Co., Eaton Corporation plc, Honeywell Aerospace Inc., Moog Inc., RTX Corporation, Safran S.A., Senior plc, Triumph Group, Inc., and Woodward, Inc.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: Across our two segments, we believe that our broad-based portfolio of core technologies, which consist of hydraulics, pneumatics, electromechanical, filtration, fluid & gas handling, process control, engineered materials, and climate control, is a positive factor in our ability to compete effectively with both large and small competitors.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Competition
text: We believe that the following factors also contribute to our ability to compete effectively: •Our business system, The Win Strategy •Technology powerhouse of interconnected solutions •Deep partnerships with our customers to develop innovative products •Application engineering expertise •Global distribution network •Decentralized operating structure

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: Certain of our operations require the use and handling of hazardous materials and, as a result, the Company is subject to United States federal, state, and local laws and regulations as well as non-U.S. laws and regulations designed to protect the environment and regulate the discharge of materials into the environment.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: These laws impose penalties, fines and other sanctions for non-compliance and liability for response costs, property damage and personal injury resulting from past and current spills, disposals or other releases of, or exposures to, hazardous materials.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: Among other environmental laws, we are subject to the United States federal "Superfund" law, under which we have been designated as a "potentially responsible party" and may be liable for cleanup costs associated with various waste sites, some of which are on the United States Environmental Protection Agency’s Superfund priority list.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: As of June 30, 2026, Parker was involved in environmental remediation and litigation at various U.S. and non-U.S. manufacturing facilities presently or formerly operated by us (or by an acquired legal entity) and as a "potentially responsible party," along with other companies, at off-site waste disposal facilities and regional sites.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: We believe that our policies, practices and procedures are properly designed to prevent unreasonable risk of environmental damage and the consequent financial liability to the Company.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Environmental Regulation
text: Compliance with environmental laws and regulations requires continuing management efforts and expenditures by the Company.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: Safety

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: The safety and well-being of Parker team members is our highest priority.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: Our safety goal is simple: to be the safest industrial company in the world, which we define as having the lowest annual recordable incident rate among our proxy peers.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: We have successfully reduced our recordable incident rate by over 50% since our fiscal year 2019.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: Our safety program is anchored on a safety management system that has globally deployed procedures and work instructions, including management of incidents and near miss events.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: We create a culture of safety through a variety of initiatives, leadership focus, and our commitment to safety as the first stated goal of The Win Strategy.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: We engage team members in improving safety performance through High Performance Teams ("HPTs").

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: All Parker manufacturing locations have an active, chartered Safety HPT and every value stream has a representative who is responsible for safety within their area of the business.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Safety
text: This ownership culture at the manufacturing level is an integral component of our safety program.

text: Engaged People

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: Engagement directly influences business performance.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: We strongly believe in empowering our team members to think like owners and take action to improve their areas of the business.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: Engagement is deeply ingrained in our culture, and as an overarching goal of The Win Strategy it is key to achieving top quartile financial performance.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: Parker activates engagement through our HPTs, which apply the expertise and perspective of team members who are closest to the product and customer to drive improvement throughout the company.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: We closely track our progress in support of a high performing work environment through our Global Engagement Survey.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Engaged People
text: Our last completed survey, in fiscal year 2025, achieved a 92% response rate with an overall engagement score of 75%.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Talent Development

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: We have a well-defined talent development program managed through our Talent Central system, which connects all business units globally on a common platform and provides team members with visibility to skill development, career planning and learning opportunities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: This shared platform is the catalyst for talent management at Parker.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Our review process enables us to assess talent globally, from early-in-career roles through senior leaders.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: This review facilitates the identification of key talent and allows us to build meaningful development plans and align career growth opportunities.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: The talent process is also supported by our Integrated Career System program which illustrates career paths for various roles and the steps to advance through the organization.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Supplementing the talent development process are Parker’s learning offerings, which help team members expand their professional skills and take ownership of their learning and development.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Examples of center-led programs are our annual ethics and compliance training and cybersecurity training that all team members are required to complete, in addition to programs for developing supervisory and leadership skills.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Functional-specific programs include HPT training, lean bootcamps and kaizen event orientations.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: Local and regional training includes site safety, equipment safety and site quality requirements.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Talent Development
text: In addition to formal training programs, there are a host of development tools available which include mentoring relationships, coaching and feedback, job shadowing, project bubble assignments and other stretch projects.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: Inclusion

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: An inclusive environment is a core tenet of our values and one of our key measures of success within The Win Strategy.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: We have an ongoing commitment to an inclusive and welcoming workplace where everyone feels valued and adds value, and different points of view are respected.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: One important component of Parker’s inclusive workplace is the development and deployment of Business Resource Groups, each of which is open to all team members.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: In addition to our Business Resource Groups, we have processes in place to attract and retain team members with a wide range of backgrounds, perspectives and experiences, helping to support them with career plans and experienced mentors.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Inclusion
text: Our goal is to promote a strong, inclusive work environment that will provide us the best talent to further strengthen our organization for success.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Compensation and Benefits
text: Compensation and Benefits

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Compensation and Benefits
text: As a global employer, we are committed to offering competitive compensation and benefits, tailored to geography, industry, experience and performance.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Compensation and Benefits
text: Our programs are designed to attract team members, motivate and reward performance, drive growth and support retention.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Compensation and Benefits
text: We provide benefit programs with the goal of improving physical, mental and financial wellness of our team members throughout their lifetime.

section_path: Part I Item 1 > Compensation and Benefits
text: Some examples include base and variable pay, health and insurance benefits, paid time off, and retirement saving plans.
